message.content: Draft the phases for the active plan "init+scout" and set them with plan_set_phases.

phases: Baseline and harness familiarization: read the init route (routes/init, engine, gates, scout step) and record how init works today; run init on one existing project to measure cost, turns, time and output quality (config.yaml, rules, scout context) as the sonnet reference.

Five synthetic init eval cases: five fixture projects on fully different stacks, generated by a script in evals/scripts (no stack-specific terms in code or prompts), each with deterministic graders on config.yaml fields, rules files and scout context; cases load and graders pass on a hand-made good result.

Sonnet baseline on the five cases: run the init cases x3 on the current setup (scout on sonnet), save per-case score, cost and turns to STATE.md as the reference to compare against; ask before the paid run.

Calibrate config.yaml assembly: fix the failing graders on config.yaml (detected profile, commands, paths) by editing the existing code or step text; the config graders pass on all five cases at least as well as the baseline, targeted tests green.

Calibrate rules collection: fix the failing graders on collected rules (relevance, no duplicates, grounded in the repo) the same way; rule graders pass on all five cases at least as well as the baseline.
Optimize init cost and speed apart from scout: remove redundant steps, reads and turns found in the traces; same or better scores at lower cost per run than the baseline on the five cases.

Scout on haiku: switch the scout subagent to haiku and compare with the saved sonnet scout results on the five cases (score, cost, funnel of context quality); keep haiku only if the scores are within the agreed tolerance, otherwise log the gap and the smallest fix to try.

Navigator regression check and wrap-up: rerun the navigator bench (6141 + 3571 + 6404 x3, then 10 cases x3 if no loss) on the new scout context and compare with haiku 932b65e4 (F1 .572); run npm run verify, bump the version, update STATE.md and commit.

file.content:
---
name: init
description: "Set up AMBICODE in this repository: .ambicode/ folder, config.yaml, policy packs, candidate rules and learning context. Run once per project."
argument-hint: "[--auto]"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(node *skills/init/scripts/*) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs config *) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs context write*) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs route start rules*) Read Write(.ambicode/config.yaml) Write(.ambicode/policies/drafts/**) Glob Grep Agent AskUserQuestion WebSearch
---
`--auto` in `$ARGUMENTS`: never ask, skip manual and web rules. Run commands plain; never poll.

1. `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs" --task init`. Exit 2: stop, tell user. `configExisted` and not `--auto`: AskUserQuestion: refresh or abort.
2. Read `.ambicode/config.yaml`. Launch `ambicode:scout` in background (`model`/`effort`: `skills.init.scout`), prompt: "Map this repo, write the context, return your report."
3. One Glob for manifests and lockfiles (depth 2), read them, derive `ecosystem`, `commands`, `checks.<name>.{all,file}` (`{file}` placeholder). Unknown stays null. Hold them for step 4; end your turn.
4. On the scout's report: `paths`, `include`, `exclude`, and per project `packs`, picked by the scout's findings from `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" config packs --list`. One Write of `.ambicode/config.yaml` (template shape; no `rules` key). `config packs --task init` copies the named built-ins to `.ambicode/policies/`. `config validate --task init`; on errors one corrective Write.
5. Rules are packs, never config. Candidates: the scout's conventions, unless `--auto` one WebSearch of core-stack practice and one AskUserQuestion for the user's own. Draft them per `references/rules.md`, then `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" route start rules --task init` (not with `--auto`); the user applies them at its table.
6. Summary: projects, packs, checks found/missing, context files, drafts waiting, open questions. Errors: `references/outcomes.md`.

Перепроверил по цели плана и по `skills/init/SKILL.md`. Основа верная: 5 стеков, сначала config и rules, scout на haiku в конце, затем проверка навигатора. Но есть ошибки, которые стоит исправить до старта.

**Фактические ошибки**
- **p1.** Я написал «прочитать route init». Такого route нет: `routes/init/init.yaml` не существует. Init — это skill со скриптами (`skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs`) и подкоманды CLI `config`. Через engine идёт только хвост: `route start rules`. Знакомство с harness, engine и routes нужно описать иначе.
- **p1.** Там стоит платный прогон init на существующем проекте. Он дублирует p3 и по правилам требует спросить вас заранее. Лучше сделать в p1 разбор кода и локальный прогон `--auto` в песочнице без затрат.
- **p2.** «Отдельный скрипт в evals/scripts» противоречит правилу «менять, а не добавлять». Сначала нужно проверить, может ли кейсы для init генерировать уже существующий `evals/scripts/cases.mjs`. Я это не проверял.

**Расхождения с целью**
- **p3.** Вы просили сохранить *результат* scout на sonnet. У меня сохраняются только оценки. Нужно сохранять ещё сами артефакты: `.ambicode/context` и report scout для каждого из 5 кейсов. С ними p7 сравнивает haiku.
- **p8.** «Потом по ним сравним навигатора». Навигатор нужно гонять на контексте, который построил haiku-scout, а не на старом. Значит, для inseer-frontend контекст генерируется в отдельную папку, а бэкап `.local-docs/context` и текущий `.ambicode/context` остаются нетронутыми. В плане этого нет.
- **p4 и p5.** Критерий «не хуже baseline» слабый, ведь цель — откалибровать. Нужно «грейдеры config и rules улучшились относительно p3, без регрессий на остальных кейсах».
- **p5.** В режиме `--auto` rules остаются черновиками в `.ambicode/policies/drafts/`: WebSearch, вопрос пользователю и route rules пропускаются. Грейдеры должны проверять именно черновики. Ручной путь eval-ами не покрывается, это нужно записать как пробел.

**Мелочи**
- p6 по сути пересекается с p4 и p5. Можно оставить его отдельной фазой, но только по трейсам p3: лишние чтения и ходы.
- Платный прогон есть в p4–p8, а «спросить перед прогоном» указано только в p3. Это общее правило, его не нужно повторять в каждой фазе.

Предлагаю заменить фазы так:

1. Разобрать init: шаги skill, `scaffold.mjs`, `config packs/validate`, scout, переход в route rules через engine. Сделать один прогон `--auto` в песочнице без затрат и записать в STATE.md, где теряются ходы и качество.
2. Сделать 5 init-кейсов на полностью разных стеках через существующий генератор, если он подходит. Ожидаемые `config.yaml` и черновики rules лежат рядом с кейсом. Грейдеры детерминированные. Кейсы загружаются.
3. Baseline на sonnet, по 3 прогона на кейс. Сохранить оценки, стоимость и ходы, а также артефакты scout (context и report) как эталон.
4. Калибровка `config.yaml`: грейдеры config лучше, чем в p3.
5. Калибровка сбора rules (черновики): грейдеры rules лучше, чем в p3.
6. Удешевить init без scout по трейсам p3: та же оценка при меньшей цене.
7. Scout на haiku: сравнить с эталоном из p3 по оценке, цене и полноте context.
8. Навигатор на контексте от haiku-scout. Контекст строится в отдельной папке, бэкап не трогается. Бенч 6141 + 3571 + 6404 по 3 прогона, затем 10 кейсов по 3, против 932b65e4 (F1 .572). Потом verify, bump, STATE.

Заменить фазы этим списком?

content.content:
---
name: init
description: "Set up AMBICODE in this repository: .ambicode/ folder, config.yaml, policy packs, candidate rules and learning context. Run once per project."
argument-hint: "[--auto]"
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(node *skills/init/scripts/*) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs config *) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs context write*) Bash(node *ambicode.mjs route start rules*) Read Write(.ambicode/config.yaml) Write(.ambicode/policies/drafts/**) Glob Grep Agent AskUserQuestion WebSearch
---
`--auto` in `$ARGUMENTS`: never ask, skip manual and web rules. Run commands plain; never poll.

1. `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs" --task init`. Exit 2: stop, tell user. `configExisted` and not `--auto`: AskUserQuestion: refresh or abort.

# Evals: skill coverage

Seventeen synthetic cases, at least one per skill, each checking one behaviour. Twelve of them also run with no
plugin loaded, which is the baseline. Every case runs on a fixture from `fixtures/definitions.mjs`, so nothing
here is real project data and the whole suite is in git. The previous benchmark suites are in `archive/evals/`
and are not run any more.

```
evals/
  scripts/cases.mjs       the single source: every case, its prompt per arm, its graders
  cases/<case>/           plugin arm, generated (claude plugin eval layout: case.yaml, prompt.md, scaffold.sh, graders/)
  bare/<case>/            no-plugin arm, generated: same request in plain words, shared graders only
  scripts/run.mjs         runs one arm through `claude plugin eval` and leaves the result in `cases/results/`
  scripts/context.mjs     reads context size, session and model seconds, and session cost from each run's trace
  scripts/trace.mjs       trace parsing and `mean`, shared by the scripts below
  scripts/metrics.mjs     recall, precision and F1 of the files an answer lists (cases that declare `metrics`)
  scripts/breakdown.mjs   where a run's calls, tokens, seconds and injected bytes go (`npm run evals:breakdown -- <trace.jsonl | dir>`)
  cases/results/          raw output of the last run per arm, and traces/<arm>/<stamp>/<case>-<n>.jsonl with the run's ledgers in `.ambicode` beside it, without the `context/` copy (gitignored)
```

## Run

```sh
npm run build                       # cases run scripts/ambicode.mjs, not src/
npm run evals                       # plugin arm: 17 cases
npm run evals:bare                  # bare arm: 12 cases, no plugin
npm run evals -- --case 'task-*'    # one skill (a glob; --case is not repeatable)
npm run evals -- --tag gate         # by tag
npm run evals -- --runs 3           # more runs per case, for a decision
npm run evals:dry                   # print both commands and change nothing
```

Defaults: Sonnet 5.5, effort low, 1 run per case, 4 runs in parallel, a $15 cap per arm. Override any of them with
`--model`, `--effort`, `--runs` or `--max-cost-usd`. The harness has no effort flag, so `run.mjs` sets
`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` in the environment. A probe showed the variable inside the run. It does not prove the
model honoured it.

Read a run in `evals/cases/results/<arm>.json` and its traces under `results/traces/<arm>/<run time>/`; the plugin-master viewer shows both.

## Navigator cases

Ten ordinary cases (`fe-vs-<id>-navigator`; the asset folders keep their `fe-vs-<id>-investigate` names) on the NDA bench repo in `../ambicode-evals-assets`, rendered by
`scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (also run by `npm run evals:generate`) into `evals/cases/navigator/` (plugin arm) and
`evals/bare/navigator/` (bare arm). Both are gitignored: they hold ticket text and truth paths. Without the assets the generator
prints one line and skips; env `NAV_BENCH`, `NAV_CASES` override the sibling-directory defaults.

```sh
npm run evals -- --tag navigator        # plugin arm, one harness call, -j 4
npm run evals:bare -- --tag navigator   # bare arm
```

- Each run starts with the bench copied into a fresh git repo and no `.ambicode/`. The plugin arm's scaffold copies the
  bench's `.ambicode/context/` back in, because the navigator reads only that; the bare scaffold copies nothing.
- The prompt is the ticket plus one instruction, the same for both arms: return the files as a ```files block. The plugin arm
  measures the navigator alone: `allowed_tools: [Agent]`, no `--allow-tools` shell grant, and an `append_system_prompt` that makes
  the session call `ambicode:navigator` once in the foreground and copy its paths unchanged (grader `navigator-called`). The harness
  has no main-agent option, and its tool lists bind subagents too, so the session keeps the read tools; the relay text forbids using them.
- Score = recall over the truth folders. The nav truth (logic files; i18n and fixtures dropped; companion files dropped except that a companion-only directory becomes a directory item) is collapsed to its unique folders, and a folder is covered when any line of the first ```files block is that folder, lies under it, or is an ancestor directory (or a file directly in one) with at least 30% of the source folders under it covered by the truth (`ancestors` in `truth.json`, computed from the bench at generation; the 0.3 is a choice, not measured). One regex grader per truth folder. Step graders (`files-block`, plugin-only `navigator-called`) weigh 0.0001 each, so
  score = (hits + 0.0001 * steps passed) / (|T| + 0.0001 * steps) is within 1e-4 of recall. Precision and F1 come from
  `truth.json` in the case dir (nav truth `relevant`, the rest `allowed`, plus `level: 'folder'`, `ancestorShare` and the `ancestors` map, which the graders and `scoreNavigator` read). `run.mjs` writes `recall`, `precision`, `f1`, `missed`, `extra` and `contract` into each run's `metrics` in the result JSON, computed by `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` from the trace's first ```files block and `truth.json`. Recall is pinned to the recall graders (passed / total); if the computed value differs, the grader value is written and `mismatch: true` is set.
- `--tag navigator` is one `claude plugin eval` call at the default `-j 4`, like any other selection: the cases share no state.
  The result goes to `cases/results/<arm>.json` and, with the metrics, to `cases/results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`
  (bare: `cases/results/bare/<stamp>/`), which the viewer reads.
- Navigator cases run only with `--tag navigator`: an unfiltered run lists the skill tags instead (the harness has no exclude option).


## Recall, precision, drift

A case with `metrics` in `cases.mjs` is scored on the files its answer lists. The prompt asks both arms for a
`## Files` section, and only that section counts, because answers also name decoys in order to rule them out.
- **Recall** is the share of the `relevant` files the list names.
- **Precision** is the share of listed files that are `relevant` or `allowed`.
- **F1** combines the two.
- Navigator cases do not use `scoreFiles` (it stays file-level, for the skill cases). `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` computes recall, precision and F1 by the folder rule and `run.mjs` writes them to the result JSON; a viewer reads them generically from `metrics`. The rule: a file counts as its directory, a truth folder is covered by an answer folder equal to or under it, or above it when at least 30% of the source folders under that ancestor (directories holding a logic file) are covered; an answer folder is correct when related the same way to a folder of `relevant` or `allowed`.

A run with no Files section scores recall 0 and F1 0, and is counted separately.

Read the result files, not the exit code. The harness exits 1 whenever any case scores below 1.0.

## /ambicode:init walkthrough (read-only; no model sessions; scratch repo in $TMPDIR/tmp.U89Mh7dOLa/repo)

**Step table** (SKILL.md has 6 steps; actor in brackets)
| step | actor | inputs -> outputs | observed issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 scaffold | code (`skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs --task init`) | git root -> `.ambicode/{tasks,reviews,context}`, `config.yaml` from `templates/config.yaml`, `.ambicode/` appended to `.gitignore`, ledger line, JSON | exit 2 if not git root. With `configExisted` and no `--auto` the model asks refresh/abort (real traces: 3 of 9 sessions). |
| 2 launch scout | model (Agent, background) | model/effort taken from `skills.init.scout` -> scout report + context files | The setting is only schema-validated in src (`types/modules/config.ts`). Nothing in code reads it; the model must copy it into the Agent call. |
| 3 manifests | model (1 Glob, reads) | manifests -> ecosystem, commands, checks | Model work done while the scout runs, then the turn ends. |
| 4 config | model Write + code | scout report, `config packs --list` -> config.yaml, `.ambicode/policies/<x>/*.yaml` | See "ignored" below. The pack list is plain text and has no stack-tag metadata. |
| 4b validate | code (`config validate --task init`) | -> `ok` or `field: msg` lines, exit 1 | Messages are clear. |
| 5 rules | model (WebSearch and AskUserQuestion unless `--auto`) then `route start rules --task init` (not with `--auto`) | scout conventions -> `.ambicode/policies/drafts/<id>.yaml` | The rules route is: discover (code), sources (human), chosen (code), draft (model), rules-table (human), apply (model). I did not run it. |
| 6 summary | model | -> final message | `references/outcomes.md` lists the errors. |

**Scout** (`agents/scout.md`): model sonnet fixed in the frontmatter; the config default is sonnet/medium/10min; tools are Bash, Read, Grep, Glob. It runs `context tree` (also `--level n` and `--index`) and writes `context write --task init --root <dir> [--replace]` bundles level by level. The last write is `index.md`. Its final message holds `projects`, `conventions` (max 10, each with a verbatim quote, location and basis), `context files` and `unknowns`. Output is `.ambicode/context/{overview,navigation,conventions,index}.md` and `modules/**.md`, size-checked by `check.problems`.

**What a case must grade**
- Deterministic (file or regex): `config.yaml` exists; `schemaVersion` 5; `projects[].paths/include/exclude/ecosystem/packs/commands/checks.*.{all,file}` with `{file}`; no `rules` key; `policies/<group>/<pack>.yaml` copied and listed; `.gitignore` has `.ambicode/`; ledger `tasks/init` has scaffold, config packs, config validate, context write; the context files exist; `config validate` exits 0.
- Needs a model grader or rubric: whether the picked packs fit the stack; whether context purposes are accurate; draft shape (`policies/drafts/*.yaml`, authority, `source.quote` of 20+ characters, which can be checked verbatim against the file at `location`); summary completeness.

**Existing generator.** `evals/scripts/cases.mjs` already has `init-auto`: fixture `ts-feature-boundary` with `--install`, `intoCwd`, prompt `/ambicode:init --auto`, 16 graders, `max_turns` 24, 900s. Its scaffold materializes the fixture into the session cwd. The generator can carry 5 cases if I add:
- 4 more fixtures in `fixtures/definitions.mjs`. There are only ts-*, py-clean-docstring and eval-* fixtures, so a python, a monorepo, a go/java-like stack and an existing-config repo are missing. Fixtures are just file maps plus `install`.
- Per-case grader sets (the stack-specific regexes are currently inline).
- A no-`--auto` variant. It needs AskUserQuestion answers, which the harness may not support. The `--auto` path is the only one gradable at $0 of human input.
- A rules-draft grader, since `--auto` skips drafts.
- Suspected gap, unverified: the `init` limits list `allowed_tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Write, Skill`, with no `Agent`, yet the `scout-invoked` grader needs Agent. I did not check how the harness treats this. Past results hold no init-auto run (only navigator traces), so there is no baseline number.

**Step 3, measured** (`ts-feature-boundary`, built with `npm run build`; `--install` left no node_modules, so it likely did nothing offline)
```
scaffold.mjs --task init        exit 0  168B  created tasks,reviews,context,config.yaml; .gitignore "added"; ledger line
config packs --list             exit 0  1662B 14+ builtin/* (angular-*, common-*, express-*, python-quality)
(wrote config: paths [src/], express, 3 packs, test+lint checks)
config packs --task init        exit 0  322B  3 pack files written; prints "ignored: none"
config validate --task init     exit 0  3B    "ok"
bad {file} placeholder          exit 1        projects.0.checks.test.file: must contain {file}
context tree --root src         1 module (src.md, 9 files)
context write (1-file bundle)   exit 0  {"written":["overview.md"],"check":{"problems":[]}}
```
Surprises:
- `config packs` rewrote my `ignored: [node_modules/]` to `[]`, because node_modules is absent on disk. A hand-written `ignored` does not survive; the value comes from disk.
- Packs went to `policies/common/` and `policies/express/`.
- `git status` shows only `.gitignore` modified. Each step logs a ledger line, including `context write`.
- `route start --help` is rejected as an unknown option.
- My first two calls failed with "Unknown command" because I quoted the subcommand as one word. That was my mistake, not the CLI's.
- Not run: the scout, the rules route, and a full-size `context write`.

**Real init traces** (`~/.claude/projects/-…-inseer-inseer-frontend/*.jsonl` plus `subagents/`, 9 sessions Oct 12–19; none under `evals/cases/results` or `gym`). Deduplicated by message id, latest three:
```
5a8f7355 (10-19) main: 10 turns, 467s wall (includes 2 AskUserQuestion waits); tools Bash4 Ask2 Read Glob Agent Write
          scout:  11 turns, 100s, Bash10 Read2
8e9b0819 (10-19) main: 10 turns, 473s; scout 13 turns, 179s
bc6427a7 (10-19) 4 scout runs: 9t/121s, 8t/100s, 56t/531s (56 Bash), 22t/232s
```
Earlier sessions (10-12 and 10-16) with WebSearch and Write: 18 and 36 assistant messages, 5 and 10 minutes. Token and cost figures are not reliable here: the scout's `output_tokens` read 100–540, which looks like partial streaming usage. I did not compute dollars.

**Top suspected inefficiencies / gaps**
1. **Measured**: scout turn count varies 8–56 on the same repo (bc6427a7). Bash calls dominate (`context tree --level`, one `context write` per level). This is the biggest cost and variance, and the 56-turn run took 531s.
2. **Measured**: the human gate (`configExisted` refresh/abort ask, and the 2 AskUserQuestion calls) accounts for most main-session wall time (about 370s of 467s). `--auto` removes it, and `init-auto` only covers `--auto`.
3. **Measured**: `config packs` overwrites `ignored`, so the model's step-4 effort on it is wasted. It also reported "ignored: none" without saying why.
4. **Guessed**: `skills.init.scout` is applied only through prose instructions, so the model can ignore it. The traces show `model:"sonnet"` passed, but I did not see effort.
5. **Guessed**: packs are picked from a plain description list with no stack-keyed metadata (the repo rule is to avoid ecosystem tables), so pack choice quality is the least gradable part.
- Not checked: the init-auto Agent allow-list question, whether the 5a8f7355 session's scout wrote the context (I did not inspect its output), and the rules-route draft quality.

# Evals: skill coverage

Seventeen synthetic cases, at least one per skill, each checking one behaviour. Twelve of them also run with no
plugin loaded, which is the baseline. Every case runs on a fixture from `fixtures/definitions.mjs`, so nothing
here is real project data and the whole suite is in git. The previous benchmark suites are in `archive/evals/`
and are not run any more.

```
evals/
  scripts/cases.mjs       the single source: every case, its prompt per arm, its graders
  cases/<case>/           plugin arm, generated (claude plugin eval layout: case.yaml, prompt.md, scaffold.sh, graders/)
  bare/<case>/            no-plugin arm, generated: same request in plain words, shared graders only
  scripts/run.mjs         runs one arm through `claude plugin eval` and leaves the result in `cases/results/`
  scripts/context.mjs     reads context size, session and model seconds, and session cost from each run's trace
  scripts/trace.mjs       trace parsing and `mean`, shared by the scripts below
  scripts/metrics.mjs     recall, precision and F1 of the files an answer lists (cases that declare `metrics`)
  scripts/breakdown.mjs   where a run's calls, tokens, seconds and injected bytes go (`npm run evals:breakdown -- <trace.jsonl | dir>`)
  cases/results/          raw output of the last run per arm, and traces/<arm>/<stamp>/<case>-<n>.jsonl with the run's ledgers in `.ambicode` beside it, without the `context/` copy (gitignored)
```

## Run

```sh
npm run build                       # cases run scripts/ambicode.mjs, not src/
npm run evals                       # plugin arm: 17 cases
npm run evals:bare                  # bare arm: 12 cases, no plugin
npm run evals -- --case 'task-*'    # one skill (a glob; --case is not repeatable)
npm run evals -- --tag gate         # by tag
npm run evals -- --runs 3           # more runs per case, for a decision
npm run evals:dry                   # print both commands and change nothing
```

Defaults: Sonnet 5.5, effort low, 1 run per case, 4 runs in parallel, a $15 cap per arm. Override any of them with
`--model`, `--effort`, `--runs` or `--max-cost-usd`. The harness has no effort flag, so `run.mjs` sets
`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` in the environment. A probe showed the variable inside the run. It does not prove the
model honoured it.

Read a run in `evals/cases/results/<arm>.json` and its traces under `results/traces/<arm>/<run time>/`; the plugin-master viewer shows both.

## Navigator cases

Ten ordinary cases (`fe-vs-<id>-navigator`; the asset folders keep their `fe-vs-<id>-investigate` names) on the NDA bench repo in `../ambicode-evals-assets`, rendered by
`scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (also run by `npm run evals:generate`) into `evals/cases/navigator/` (plugin arm) and
`evals/bare/navigator/` (bare arm). Both are gitignored: they hold ticket text and truth paths. Without the assets the generator
prints one line and skips; env `NAV_BENCH`, `NAV_CASES` override the sibling-directory defaults.

```sh
npm run evals -- --tag navigator        # plugin arm, one harness call, -j 4
npm run evals:bare -- --tag navigator   # bare arm
```

- Each run starts with the bench copied into a fresh git repo and no `.ambicode/`. The plugin arm's scaffold copies the
  bench's `.ambicode/context/` back in, because the navigator reads only that; the bare scaffold copies nothing.
- The prompt is the ticket plus one instruction, the same for both arms: return the files as a ```files block. The plugin arm
  measures the navigator alone: `allowed_tools: [Agent]`, no `--allow-tools` shell grant, and an `append_system_prompt` that makes
  the session call `ambicode:navigator` once in the foreground and copy its paths unchanged (grader `navigator-called`). The harness
  has no main-agent option, and its tool lists bind subagents too, so the session keeps the read tools; the relay text forbids using them.
- Score = recall over the truth folders. The nav truth (logic files; i18n and fixtures dropped; companion files dropped except that a companion-only directory becomes a directory item) is collapsed to its unique folders, and a folder is covered when any line of the first ```files block is that folder, lies under it, or is an ancestor directory (or a file directly in one) with at least 30% of the source folders under it covered by the truth (`ancestors` in `truth.json`, computed from the bench at generation; the 0.3 is a choice, not measured). One regex grader per truth folder. Step graders (`files-block`, plugin-only `navigator-called`) weigh 0.0001 each, so
  score = (hits + 0.0001 * steps passed) / (|T| + 0.0001 * steps) is within 1e-4 of recall. Precision and F1 come from
  `truth.json` in the case dir (nav truth `relevant`, the rest `allowed`, plus `level: 'folder'`, `ancestorShare` and the `ancestors` map, which the graders and `scoreNavigator` read). `run.mjs` writes `recall`, `precision`, `f1`, `missed`, `extra` and `contract` into each run's `metrics` in the result JSON, computed by `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` from the trace's first ```files block and `truth.json`. Recall is pinned to the recall graders (passed / total); if the computed value differs, the grader value is written and `mismatch: true` is set.
- `--tag navigator` is one `claude plugin eval` call at the default `-j 4`, like any other selection: the cases share no state.
  The result goes to `cases/results/<arm>.json` and, with the metrics, to `cases/results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`
  (bare: `cases/results/bare/<stamp>/`), which the viewer reads.
- Navigator cases run only with `--tag navigator`: an unfiltered run lists the skill tags instead (the harness has no exclude option).


## Recall, precision, drift

A case with `metrics` in `cases.mjs` is scored on the files its answer lists. The prompt asks both arms for a
`## Files` section, and only that section counts, because answers also name decoys in order to rule them out.
- **Recall** is the share of the `relevant` files the list names.
- **Precision** is the share of listed files that are `relevant` or `allowed`.
- **F1** combines the two.
- Navigator cases do not use `scoreFiles` (it stays file-level, for the skill cases). `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` computes recall, precision and F1 by the folder rule and `run.mjs` writes them to the result JSON; a viewer reads them generically from `metrics`. The rule: a file counts as its directory, a truth folder is covered by an answer folder equal to or under it, or above it when at least 30% of the source folders under that ancestor (directories holding a logic file) are covered; an answer folder is correct when related the same way to a folder of `relevant` or `allowed`.

A run with no Files section scores recall 0 and F1 0, and is counted separately.

Read the result files, not the exit code. The harness exits 1 whenever any case scores below 1.0.

## How a case works

1. **Scaffold.** `scaffold.sh` replays a fixture into `repo/`, a fresh git repository with known history. The
   plugin arm also commits `.ambicode/config.yaml`. `--install` fixtures run `npm ci`, so jest and eslint are real. `--context` also writes
   `fixtures/contexts/<fixture>.md` into the gitignored `.ambicode/context`, standing in for the scout (8 of the 17 cases).
2. **Prompt.** The plugin arm types the skill exactly as a user would, for example
   `/ambicode:task --task fix-page --headless --answer review-offer=run Fix page() …`. `--task` fixes the slug so
   graders can find the ledger. `--answer` pre-answers a gate. A case with no answer tests the gate's default. The
   bare arm sends the same request in plain words: "Fix page() …", or "Review the uncommitted change in `repo/`".
3. **Graders.** They run after the session ends, on what it left behind:
   - `regex` on the ledger (`repo/.ambicode/tasks/<slug>/ledger.jsonl`), on a produced file, or on the final message.
   - `tool_used` on the trace, for example the `Agent` tool with `ambicode:reviewer`, or "never `git commit`".
   - `file_exists` for files the run created.
   - `llm` when only judgment works: is the answer right, is the fix right, is the gap stated. Haiku judges with
     three votes.
4. **Score.** The weighted share of graders that passed.

## Plugin against bare

Graders come in two kinds:

- **Shared graders** judge the outcome: the answer, the code, the review finding, the boundary (no edits, no git).
  They run in both arms.
- **Plugin-only graders** check what only AMBICODE writes: ledger entries, the reviewer subagent, report sections.
  They run in the plugin arm only.

Five cases have no bare arm because what they test belongs to the plugin: a gate default (`plan-draft`,
`task-review-skipped`, `review-skipped`), policy packs (`rules-migrate`) and `init-auto`.

`--auto` in `$ARGUMENTS`: never ask, skip manual and web rules. Run commands plain; never poll.

1. `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs" --task init`. Exit 2: stop, tell user. `configExisted` and not `--auto`: AskUserQuestion: refresh or abort.
2. Read `.ambicode/config.yaml`. Launch `ambicode:scout` in background (`model`/`effort`: `skills.init.scout`), prompt: "Map this repo, write the context, return your report."
3. One Glob for manifests and lockfiles (depth 2), read them, derive `ecosystem`, `commands`, `checks.<name>.{all,file}` (`{file}` placeholder). Unknown stays null. Hold them for step 4; end your turn.
4. On the scout's report: `paths`, `include`, `exclude`, and per project `packs`, picked by the scout's findings from `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" config packs --list`. One Write of `.ambicode/config.yaml` (template shape; no `rules` key). `config packs --task init` copies the named built-ins to `.ambicode/policies/`. `config validate --task init`; on errors one corrective Write.
5. Rules are packs, never config. Candidates: the scout's conventions, unless `--auto` one WebSearch of core-stack practice and one AskUserQuestion for the user's own. Draft them per `references/rules.md`, then `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" route start rules --task init` (not with `--auto`); the user applies them at its table.
6. Summary: projects, packs, checks found/missing, context files, drafts waiting, open questions. Errors: `references/outcomes.md`.

---
name: scout
description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---
You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Follow this recipe exactly.

Walk the tree breadth-first: all folders of one level before any deeper. Visit each directory at most once in the whole run: keep a running list of visited directories and move on to one not on it. Locate names and files with Grep and Glob first; read content only when search results do not settle a module's purpose.

Never read a file whole (except the format spec in step 1): only heads or ranges with a line limit. Never read styles, tests or specs, mocks or fixtures, stories, nor generated, vendored, lock or build files.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only as heads with limit <= 40, only non-excluded ones, and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names and search. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language string catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms.
5. Level info, once per level before you write it: Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --level <n>` (the same roots as step 3; the roots' modules are level 1). It prints, for every folder of that level, a linked folder line and one line per unique file base name (the file name without the suffixes after its first dot) with the entity names its files declare; tests, stories, mocks, styles and templates are left out. Use it for each folder's purpose together with the heads you read.
6. Write level by level. After you have gathered one breadth-first level, write that level's notes, plus `overview.md` and `navigation.md` updated for everything seen so far (never `index.md` here), then go to the next level. Each write is one call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec and the same roots as step 3. The first write adds `--replace`; later writes omit it, so they add or update only the files in their bundle and keep the rest. `index.md` links may name only notes already written or in that bundle. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: fix those notes from what you just read and write that level again before going deeper. Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

`## Purpose` has 2 bullets of at most 25 words each: the first says what the folder is for in the product's own words (the titles and abbreviations read in step 4, the entity names from step 5), the second says what roles it contains (the kinds of things its subfolders and base names are); neither restates the folder name or says "source files of ... scope". Write `## Key files` and `## Folders` as empty headings: `context write` fills them from the code, and it generates the `Root:` field, so write paths relative to the module directory or none. To describe a file, repeat its generated bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares; to describe a folded folder, repeat its generated bullet as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>`. Each description is at most 12 words and comes from the names and level info only, with no extra file reads.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>` (the full note path is accepted: `context write` makes it relative), so a reader can find it from the parent. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

`index.md` is the folder tree the spec describes: its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, and where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Build it from the output of Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --index` (the same roots): it prints the whole `index.md` body within the `context.maxIndexTokens` budget: one line per module folder with the first Purpose bullet of its note and the names of its Key files, shallowest levels first, so every note it links must already be written. Copy it as printed and add nothing else. Run it only after the last level's notes are written, then write `index.md` alone in one more `context write` call (no `--replace`), so every description is read from a written note.

Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is for the commands in steps 2, 3 and 5 (`git ls-files`, `context tree` with and without `--level` or `--index`), the `context write` in step 6, and plain read-only listing (`ls`, `git ls-files`). Use Glob for file lookup.

Final message (returned to the caller, not written to disk), compact:
- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from tidewatch.errors import StaleReadingError, UnknownGaugeError
from tidewatch.models import Reading
from tidewatch.store import READINGS

MAX_AGE = timedelta(minutes=45)


def latest_reading(gauge_id: str, *, now: datetime) -> Reading:
    readings = READINGS.get(gauge_id)
    if not readings:
        raise UnknownGaugeError("TW-101", f"no gauge named {gauge_id}")
    newest = max(readings, key=lambda item: item.taken_at)
    if now - newest.taken_at > MAX_AGE:
        raise StaleReadingError("TW-203", f"gauge {gauge_id} last reported {newest.taken_at.isoformat()}")
    return newest

import math
from datetime import datetime

from tidewatch.errors import WindowTooLongError
from tidewatch.gauges import latest_reading
from tidewatch.models import Window

MAX_HOURS = 48
SWING_MM = 300


def _swing(hour: int) -> int:
    return int(SWING_MM * math.sin(hour * math.pi / 6.2))


def forecast_window(gauge_id: str, *, start: datetime, hours: int) -> Window:
    if hours > MAX_HOURS:
        raise WindowTooLongError("TW-310", f"{hours} hours asked, at most {MAX_HOURS}")
    base = latest_reading(gauge_id, now=start)
    heights = tuple(base.level_mm + _swing(hour) for hour in range(hours))
    return Window(gauge_id=gauge_id, start=start, hourly_mm=heights)

from datetime import datetime

from tidewatch.errors import TidewatchError
from tidewatch.forecast import forecast_window
from tidewatch.gauges import latest_reading


def current_level(gauge_id: str, *, now: datetime) -> dict:
    try:
        reading = latest_reading(gauge_id, now=now)
    except TidewatchError as error:
        return {"ok": False, "code": error.code}
    return {"ok": True, "level_mm": reading.level_mm}


def tide_window(gauge_id: str, *, start: datetime, hours: int) -> dict:
    try:
        window = forecast_window(gauge_id, start=start, hours=hours)
    except TidewatchError as error:
        return {"ok": False, "code": error.code}
    return {"ok": True, "hourly_mm": list(window.hourly_mm)}

import math
from datetime import datetime

from tidewatch.errors import WindowTooLongError
from tidewatch.gauges import latest_reading
from tidewatch.models import Window

MAX_HOURS = 48
SWING_MM = 300


def _swing(hour: int) -> int:
    return int(SWING_MM * math.sin(hour * math.pi / 6.2))


def forecast_window(gauge_id: str, *, start: datetime, hours: int) -> Window:
    if hours > MAX_HOURS:
        raise WindowTooLongError("TW-310", f"{hours} hours asked, at most {MAX_HOURS}")
    base = latest_reading(gauge_id, now=start)
    heights = tuple(base.level_mm + _swing(hour) for hour in range(hours))
    return Window(gauge_id=gauge_id, start=start, hourly_mm=heights)

package org.seedvault.catalog

import org.seedvault.LotId
import org.seedvault.Outcome
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory

class Catalog {
    private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(Catalog::class.java)
    private val lots = mutableMapOf<LotId, SeedLot>()

    fun register(lot: SeedLot): Outcome<SeedLot> {
        if (lot.id in lots) return Outcome.Rejected("lot ${lot.id.value} is already registered")
        lots[lot.id] = lot
        log.atInfo().addKeyValue("lotId", lot.id.value).addKeyValue("viability", lot.viabilityPercent).log("lot.registered")
        return Outcome.Ok(lot)
    }

    fun find(id: LotId): Outcome<SeedLot> {
        val lot = lots[id] ?: return Outcome.Rejected("no lot named ${id.value}")
        return Outcome.Ok(lot)
    }

    fun all(): List<SeedLot> = lots.values.toList()
}

package org.seedvault.germination

import org.seedvault.LotId
import org.seedvault.Outcome
import org.seedvault.catalog.Catalog
import org.seedvault.catalog.SeedLot
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory
import java.time.Clock
import java.time.LocalDate

const val MIN_VIABILITY_PERCENT = 50
const val MAX_AGE_YEARS = 10L

data class Sowing(val lot: SeedLot, val trays: Int)

class Germination(private val catalog: Catalog, private val clock: Clock) {
    private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(Germination::class.java)

    fun sow(id: LotId, trays: Int): Outcome<Sowing> {
        val lot = when (val found = catalog.find(id)) {
            is Outcome.Ok -> found.value
            is Outcome.Rejected -> return found
        }
        val today = LocalDate.now(clock)
        if (lot.viabilityPercent < MIN_VIABILITY_PERCENT) return Outcome.Rejected("lot ${id.value} is below $MIN_VIABILITY_PERCENT% viability")
        if (lot.storedOn.plusYears(MAX_AGE_YEARS).isBefore(today)) return Outcome.Rejected("lot ${id.value} is older than $MAX_AGE_YEARS years")
        log.atInfo().addKeyValue("lotId", id.value).addKeyValue("trays", trays).log("lot.sown")
        return Outcome.Ok(Sowing(lot, trays))
    }
}

- Not done: no paid run, and no drafts for the TS case.

## Navigator: where we are (2026-10-20)

Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plan: "navigator eval" (3146e432), next phase p12 (cleanup). Child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397) completed 2026-10-20.

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.

# AMBICODE configuration. Written by /ambicode:init; edit freely, then run:

schemaVersion: 5
id: cwd
baseline: origin/main # branch review needs it or --base
context:
  # limits for .ambicode/context (tokens = chars / 4)
  maxTotalTokens: 60000
  maxFileTokens: 2500
  maxIndexTokens: 5000 # index.md alone; still counts toward maxTotalTokens
skills:
  # every skill: model, effort, timeoutMinutes, plus its own keys
  init:
    model: sonnet
    effort: medium
    timeoutMinutes: 20
    scout: { model: sonnet, effort: medium, timeoutMinutes: 10 }
  review:
    model: sonnet
    effort: medium
    timeoutMinutes: 15
    maxFindings: null
    maxChangedFiles: null
    maxChangedLines: null
    maxContextBytes: null
    excludePaths: []
  task: { model: sonnet, effort: medium, timeoutMinutes: 60, checkTimeoutSeconds: 120 }
  plan: { model: sonnet, effort: medium, timeoutMinutes: 30 }
  investigate: { model: sonnet, effort: low, timeoutMinutes: 15 }
  rules: { model: sonnet, effort: medium, timeoutMinutes: 15 }
requirements:
  runtimes: {} # node: ">=20"
  mcps: [] # MCP server names; the first Jira/Confluence one is the requirements server
  lsps: []
  env: [] # names only
projects:
  - id: dashboard
    root: dashboard
    paths: [ dashboard ]
    ecosystem: { languages: [ typescript ], frameworks: [ express ], packageManager: npm }
    include: [ "dashboard/**/*.ts" ]
    exclude: [ "**/node_modules/**", "**/*.test.ts" ]
    ignored: []
    packs: [ builtin/common-checks, builtin/common-code, builtin/common-design, builtin/common-errors, builtin/common-security, builtin/common-verification, builtin/express-errors, builtin/express-http, builtin/express-persistence ]
    policyFiles: [ .ambicode/policies/common/common-checks.yaml, .ambicode/policies/common/common-code.yaml, .ambicode/policies/common/common-design.yaml, .ambicode/policies/common/common-errors.yaml, .ambicode/policies/common/common-security.yaml, .ambicode/policies/common/common-verification.yaml, .ambicode/policies/express/express-errors.yaml, .ambicode/policies/express/express-http.yaml, .ambicode/policies/express/express-persistence.yaml ]
    commands: { dev: "npm run dev", build: "npm run build" }
    checks:
      test: { all: "npm test", file: "npx vitest run {file}" }
      lint: { all: "npm run lint", file: "npx eslint {file}" }
      build: { all: "npm run build", file: null }
  - id: engine

    paths: [ engine ]

packaged as one tool, **no Bash** (too risky). Context exists only to make the navigator faster/cheaper; dropping it is a later decision.
Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plan: "navigator eval" (3146e432), next phase p12 (cleanup). Child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397) completed 2026-10-20.

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.

Пробный прогон прошёл без сбоев harness и стоил $0.89 вместо выделенных $8. Средняя оценка 0.854.

```
case       score  cost    main turns  scout (sonnet)  time
ts         .923   $0.207  4           9 calls         50s
python     .871   $0.158  4           8               50s
go         .759   $0.171  4           9               59s
jvm        .862   $0.166  4           10              54s
monorepo   .857   $0.190  4           9               52s
```

**Реальные проблемы init (для p20/p21, до baseline их не чиню):**
- **Черновики rules не создаются.** В 4 кейсах с конвенциями `--auto` не записал ни одного черновика: модель считает, что флаг отменяет и этот шаг, хотя по шагу 5 skill черновики должны быть. На это приходится 16 из 17 упавших грейдеров вне ts и судьи go.
- **go.** Scout не прочитал `CONTRIBUTING.md` и не создал `conventions.md`. Из checks выпал `golangci-lint`, хотя он есть в README.
- **monorepo.** У Rust-проекта нет проверки `cargo clippy`.
- **ts.** llm-судья трижды поставил FAIL, а по тексту ответа критерии выглядят выполненными. Почему, неясно: harness не сохраняет рассуждения судьи.

**Что мешает baseline:**
1. **Контекст scout не сохраняется.** Harness специально не копирует `.ambicode/context/*` в трейсы, поэтому эталон sonnet для сравнения с haiku в p23 сейчас записать невозможно. Нужна небольшая правка `run.mjs`, бесплатная, чтобы он копировал `context/`. Это примерно 10 файлов на прогон, лимит каталога 20 000 не под угрозой: сейчас там 11 734 файла.
2. **Fixtures маленькие.** На них scout тратит около 9 вызовов, а на inseer-frontend от 8 до 56. Возможно, на таких кейсах разница между haiku и sonnet не проявится. Это скорее довод проверять haiku и на inseer-frontend: часть p24 так и устроена.

Предлагаю:
- **а) Сохранение контекста.** Поправить `run.mjs`, чтобы он сохранял `context/` в трейсы. Это $0, коммит.
- **б) Baseline ×3.** Прогнать все 5 кейсов по 3 раза в текущем виде, черновики не трогать, это задача p21. Ориентир около $2.7, ставлю лимит **$4**.

Запускать а) и б)?

  - ts: 0.114/0.133/0.135

  - go: 0.123/0.120/0.123
  - jvm: 0.127/0.127/0.130
  - monorepo: 0.162/0.143/0.141

  - `ecosystem` 2/3 (pattern not in config.yaml): init gap or grader issue. I did not check which.

  - `drafts-written` 3/3, plus `draft-outcome-not-exceptions`, `draft-structured-log-keys` and `draft-value-class-ids` 3/3 each (Write 0x): init gap.
  - `root-or-paths` 2/3 (pattern not in config.yaml): init gap or grader issue. I did not check which.

  - `drafts-written` 3/3, plus `draft-deci-celsius-names`, `draft-invariant-expect` and `draft-register-app-routes` 3/3 each (Write 0x): init gap.
  - `lint-check-engine` 1/3 (pattern not in config.yaml): init gap or grader issue. I did not check which.
  - `summary-and-pack-fit` 1/3 (judge PASS FAIL FAIL): init gap.
- No harness failures: every run got a trace and a scored result.
- The `drafts-written` failure is systematic across all four non-ts cases (Write 0x in every run).

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted

Дочерний план «scout on haiku» создан и активен, он висит под фазой p23 основного плана. В нём 5 фаз:

1. **Профиль scout и мера качества ($0).** По трейсам p19 и реальному трейсу на inseer-frontend разложу, на что уходят ходы и токены scout. Добавлю в кейсы init детерминированные грейдеры контекста:
   - покрыты ли все модули;
   - есть ли заложенные конвенции в `conventions.md`;
   - полон ли `index.md`.

   Этими грейдерами оценю эталон sonnet.
2. **Модель scout задаётся только конфигом.** Сейчас `sonnet` жёстко прописан в `agents/scout.md`, а `skills.init.scout` модель передаёт только по тексту инструкции. Это нужно исправить и покрыть тестом.
3. **Haiku без правок:** 5 кейсов ×3 против эталона sonnet.
4. **Минимальная правка под главный пробел haiku** и сокращение лишних ходов, затем повторный прогон ×3.
5. **Проверка на большом репозитории.** Haiku-scout строит контекст inseer-frontend в отдельную папку, бэкап не трогаем. Этот контекст потом пойдёт в регрессию навигатора.

На вопросы 1–3 ответа ещё нет: перенос старых результатов в архив запущен и пока идёт. Это перенос, не удаление. Субагент сначала соберёт опись `evals/cases/results/`: какие там группы прогонов, сколько в каждой записей и что лежит в одном трейсе. Архив он положит в `.local-docs/eval-archive/`, если `.local-docs` в git-ignore, иначе в отдельную папку рядом с репозиторием. Сегодняшние прогоны init останутся на месте, их метки записаны в STATE.md. Когда он закончит, отвечу на вопросы 1 и 2 и начну p1 дочернего плана.

**Measure.** I found no 20,000-entry rule in `evals/README.md` or `run.mjs`, so I used plain `find evals | wc -l`. Your ~19,032 figure doesn't match anything I counted. `evals/cases/` alone was 19,033 and `evals/` total was 19,389.

**Inventory** (all under `evals/cases/results/`; entries = `find` count)

| Group | Cases | Stamps | Entries |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<stamp>/` (aggregate-result.json + report.html) | navigator `fe-vs-*`, 82 stamps | 2026-10-19T20-53 to 2026-10-20T18-12 | about 330 |
| `<stamp>/` | 5 stamps on 13-07 to 13-09 (`--runs 2` runs of 6141-navigator) | 2026-10-20 | included above |

| `bare/<stamp>/` (aggregate copy only) | navigator, 10 stamps | 2026-10-19T20-17 to 20-24 | 21 |
| `traces/bare/<stamp>/` | navigator (`fe-vs-*-N.jsonl`), 10 stamps | 2026-10-19 | 41 |
| top-level `plugin.json`, `bare.json` and 4 `.bak` files (KEPT) | n/a | n/a | 6 |

There were no task-lifecycle or older non-navigator stamps. Navigator stamps are 82 of the 92, and the other 10 are init.

**What one trace holds.** `traces/plugin/<stamp>/<case>-N.jsonl` is the transcript. Next to it, `<case>-N.ambicode/` is the kept `.ambicode/`. That includes `config.yaml`, `policies/` and `tasks/<task>/ledger.jsonl`. The `.ambicode/` copies hold nearly all the entries. A navigator stamp averages roughly 200 entries, mostly the context index. Bare traces are just the jsonl files. `<stamp>/report.html` and `aggregate-result.json` are the viewer copies. I saw no separate context folder.

**Archive path.** `/Users/KillBill/Documents/projects/mine/ai/ambicode/.local-docs/eval-archive/`. It is ignored by `~/.gitignore_global` line 10 (`git check-ignore` confirmed). `.local-docs/` did not exist beforehand, so I did not touch `.local-docs/context`. The layout is preserved, for example `eval-archive/evals/cases/results/traces/plugin/<stamp>/`.

**Kept in place.**
- The 10 init stamps, in both `results/<stamp>` and `traces/plugin/<stamp>`.
- `plugin.json`, `bare.json` and their `.bak` files. `run.mjs` writes the first two as the run output.
- `evals/history.jsonl` (33 lines). It sits outside the results dir and I did not move it.
- Nothing in `evals/scripts`, `src` or `tools` reads older stamps. `run.mjs` only writes the per-stamp copies. `cases.mjs` and `suite.test.mjs` merely skip the `results` directory when listing cases. I could not inspect the external evals viewer, so I can't say whether it expects the moved stamps.

**Counts**

```
before: evals 19389, results 18405
moved:  184 top-level items, 17862 entries
after:  evals 1527, results 543, archive 17870
```

The archive is 8 entries larger than the moved set because of the parent directories `mkdir -p` created. 1527 + 17862 = 19389, so the totals match.

**Verification.**
- All 10 init stamps are present in both `results/` and `traces/plugin/`.
- `results/bare` and `traces/bare` are now empty directories.
- `git status` shows no changes under `evals/cases/results`, because that directory is ignored. The only changes are the earlier `.plugin-master` ones (`STATE.md`, `plans/d4d08796.json`, the run files), plus `config.json` and an untracked `plans/d4083a5a.json` that I did not touch.
- I never went near the inseer bench backup, so I ran no `cmp` on it.

The move script is `/tmp/mv/m.sh`.

---
name: scout
description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---
You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Follow this recipe exactly.

Walk the tree breadth-first: all folders of one level before any deeper. Visit each directory at most once in the whole run: keep a running list of visited directories and move on to one not on it. Locate names and files with Grep and Glob first; read content only when search results do not settle a module's purpose.

Never read a file whole (except the format spec in step 1): only heads or ranges with a line limit. Never read styles, tests or specs, mocks or fixtures, stories, nor generated, vendored, lock or build files.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only as heads with limit <= 40, only non-excluded ones, and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names and search. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language string catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms.
5. Level info, once per level before you write it: Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --level <n>` (the same roots as step 3; the roots' modules are level 1). It prints, for every folder of that level, a linked folder line and one line per unique file base name (the file name without the suffixes after its first dot) with the entity names its files declare; tests, stories, mocks, styles and templates are left out. Use it for each folder's purpose together with the heads you read.
6. Write level by level. After you have gathered one breadth-first level, write that level's notes, plus `overview.md` and `navigation.md` updated for everything seen so far (never `index.md` here), then go to the next level. Each write is one call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec and the same roots as step 3. The first write adds `--replace`; later writes omit it, so they add or update only the files in their bundle and keep the rest. `index.md` links may name only notes already written or in that bundle. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: fix those notes from what you just read and write that level again before going deeper. Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

`## Purpose` has 2 bullets of at most 25 words each: the first says what the folder is for in the product's own words (the titles and abbreviations read in step 4, the entity names from step 5), the second says what roles it contains (the kinds of things its subfolders and base names are); neither restates the folder name or says "source files of ... scope". Write `## Key files` and `## Folders` as empty headings: `context write` fills them from the code, and it generates the `Root:` field, so write paths relative to the module directory or none. To describe a file, repeat its generated bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares; to describe a folded folder, repeat its generated bullet as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>`. Each description is at most 12 words and comes from the names and level info only, with no extra file reads.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>` (the full note path is accepted: `context write` makes it relative), so a reader can find it from the parent. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

`index.md` is the folder tree the spec describes: its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, and where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Build it from the output of Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --index` (the same roots): it prints the whole `index.md` body within the `context.maxIndexTokens` budget: one line per module folder with the first Purpose bullet of its note and the names of its Key files, shallowest levels first, so every note it links must already be written. Copy it as printed and add nothing else. Run it only after the last level's notes are written, then write `index.md` alone in one more `context write` call (no `--replace`), so every description is read from a written note.

Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is for the commands in steps 2, 3 and 5 (`git ls-files`, `context tree` with and without `--level` or `--index`), the `context write` in step 6, and plain read-only listing (`ls`, `git ls-files`). Use Glob for file lookup.

Final message (returned to the caller, not written to disk), compact:
- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).

# Evals: skill coverage

Twenty-one synthetic cases, at least one per skill, each checking one behaviour. Twelve of them also run with no
plugin loaded, which is the baseline. Every case runs on a fixture from `fixtures/definitions.mjs`, so nothing
here is real project data and the whole suite is in git. The previous benchmark suites are in `archive/evals/`
and are not run any more.

```
evals/
  scripts/cases.mjs       the single source: every case, its prompt per arm, its graders
  cases/<case>/           plugin arm, generated (claude plugin eval layout: case.yaml, prompt.md, scaffold.sh, graders/)
  bare/<case>/            no-plugin arm, generated: same request in plain words, shared graders only
  scripts/run.mjs         runs one arm through `claude plugin eval` and leaves the result in `cases/results/`
  scripts/context.mjs     reads context size, session and model seconds, and session cost from each run's trace
  scripts/trace.mjs       trace parsing and `mean`, shared by the scripts below
  scripts/metrics.mjs     recall, precision and F1 of the files an answer lists (cases that declare `metrics`)
  scripts/breakdown.mjs   where a run's calls, tokens, seconds and injected bytes go (`npm run evals:breakdown -- <trace.jsonl | dir>`)
  cases/results/          raw output of the last run per arm, and traces/<arm>/<stamp>/<case>-<n>.jsonl with the run's ledgers in `.ambicode` beside it, `context/` included (gitignored)
```

## Run

```sh
npm run build                       # cases run scripts/ambicode.mjs, not src/
npm run evals                       # plugin arm: 21 cases
npm run evals:bare                  # bare arm: 12 cases, no plugin
npm run evals -- --case 'task-*'    # one skill (a glob; --case is not repeatable)
npm run evals -- --tag gate         # by tag
npm run evals -- --runs 3           # more runs per case, for a decision
npm run evals:dry                   # print both commands and change nothing
```

Defaults: Sonnet 5.5, effort low, 1 run per case, 4 runs in parallel, a $15 cap per arm. Override any of them with
`--model`, `--effort`, `--runs` or `--max-cost-usd`. The harness has no effort flag, so `run.mjs` sets
`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` in the environment. A probe showed the variable inside the run. It does not prove the
model honoured it.

Read a run in `evals/cases/results/<arm>.json` and its traces under `results/traces/<arm>/<run time>/`; the plugin-master viewer shows both.

## Navigator cases

Ten ordinary cases (`fe-vs-<id>-navigator`; the asset folders keep their `fe-vs-<id>-investigate` names) on the NDA bench repo in `../ambicode-evals-assets`, rendered by
`scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (also run by `npm run evals:generate`) into `evals/cases/navigator/` (plugin arm) and
`evals/bare/navigator/` (bare arm). Both are gitignored: they hold ticket text and truth paths. Without the assets the generator
prints one line and skips; env `NAV_BENCH`, `NAV_CASES` override the sibling-directory defaults.

```sh
npm run evals -- --tag navigator        # plugin arm, one harness call, -j 4
npm run evals:bare -- --tag navigator   # bare arm
```

- Each run starts with the bench copied into a fresh git repo and no `.ambicode/`. The plugin arm's scaffold copies the
  bench's `.ambicode/context/` back in, because the navigator reads only that; the bare scaffold copies nothing.
- The prompt is the ticket plus one instruction, the same for both arms: return the files as a ```files block. The plugin arm
  measures the navigator alone: `allowed_tools: [Agent]`, no `--allow-tools` shell grant, and an `append_system_prompt` that makes
  the session call `ambicode:navigator` once in the foreground and copy its paths unchanged (grader `navigator-called`). The harness
  has no main-agent option, and its tool lists bind subagents too, so the session keeps the read tools; the relay text forbids using them.
- Score = recall over the truth folders. The nav truth (logic files; i18n and fixtures dropped; companion files dropped except that a companion-only directory becomes a directory item) is collapsed to its unique folders, and a folder is covered when any line of the first ```files block is that folder, lies under it, or is an ancestor directory (or a file directly in one) with at least 30% of the source folders under it covered by the truth (`ancestors` in `truth.json`, computed from the bench at generation; the 0.3 is a choice, not measured). One regex grader per truth folder. Step graders (`files-block`, plugin-only `navigator-called`) weigh 0.0001 each, so
  score = (hits + 0.0001 * steps passed) / (|T| + 0.0001 * steps) is within 1e-4 of recall. Precision and F1 come from
  `truth.json` in the case dir (nav truth `relevant`, the rest `allowed`, plus `level: 'folder'`, `ancestorShare` and the `ancestors` map, which the graders and `scoreNavigator` read). `run.mjs` writes `recall`, `precision`, `f1`, `missed`, `extra` and `contract` into each run's `metrics` in the result JSON, computed by `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` from the trace's first ```files block and `truth.json`. Recall is pinned to the recall graders (passed / total); if the computed value differs, the grader value is written and `mismatch: true` is set.
- `--tag navigator` is one `claude plugin eval` call at the default `-j 4`, like any other selection: the cases share no state.
  The result goes to `cases/results/<arm>.json` and, with the metrics, to `cases/results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`
  (bare: `cases/results/bare/<stamp>/`), which the viewer reads.
- Navigator cases run only with `--tag navigator`: an unfiltered run lists the skill tags instead (the harness has no exclude option).


## Recall, precision, drift

A case with `metrics` in `cases.mjs` is scored on the files its answer lists. The prompt asks both arms for a
`## Files` section, and only that section counts, because answers also name decoys in order to rule them out.
- **Recall** is the share of the `relevant` files the list names.
- **Precision** is the share of listed files that are `relevant` or `allowed`.
- **F1** combines the two.
- Navigator cases do not use `scoreFiles` (it stays file-level, for the skill cases). `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` computes recall, precision and F1 by the folder rule and `run.mjs` writes them to the result JSON; a viewer reads them generically from `metrics`. The rule: a file counts as its directory, a truth folder is covered by an answer folder equal to or under it, or above it when at least 30% of the source folders under that ancestor (directories holding a logic file) are covered; an answer folder is correct when related the same way to a folder of `relevant` or `allowed`.

A run with no Files section scores recall 0 and F1 0, and is counted separately.

Read the result files, not the exit code. The harness exits 1 whenever any case scores below 1.0.

## How a case works

1. **Scaffold.** `scaffold.sh` replays a fixture into `repo/`, a fresh git repository with known history. The
   plugin arm also commits `.ambicode/config.yaml`. `--install` fixtures run `npm ci`, so jest and eslint are real. `--context` also writes
   `fixtures/contexts/<fixture>.md` into the gitignored `.ambicode/context`, standing in for the scout (8 of the 21 cases).
2. **Prompt.** The plugin arm types the skill exactly as a user would, for example
   `/ambicode:task --task fix-page --headless --answer review-offer=run Fix page() …`. `--task` fixes the slug so
   graders can find the ledger. `--answer` pre-answers a gate. A case with no answer tests the gate's default. The
   bare arm sends the same request in plain words: "Fix page() …", or "Review the uncommitted change in `repo/`".
3. **Graders.** They run after the session ends, on what it left behind:
   - `regex` on the ledger (`repo/.ambicode/tasks/<slug>/ledger.jsonl`), on a produced file, or on the final message.
   - `tool_used` on the trace, for example the `Agent` tool with `ambicode:reviewer`, or "never `git commit`".
   - `file_exists` for files the run created.
   - `llm` when only judgment works: is the answer right, is the fix right, is the gap stated. Haiku judges with
     three votes.
4. **Score.** The weighted share of graders that passed.

## Plugin against bare

Graders come in two kinds:

- **Shared graders** judge the outcome: the answer, the code, the review finding, the boundary (no edits, no git).
  They run in both arms.
- **Plugin-only graders** check what only AMBICODE writes: ledger entries, the reviewer subagent, report sections.
  They run in the plugin arm only.

Nine cases have no bare arm because what they test belongs to the plugin: a gate default (`plan-draft`,
`task-review-skipped`, `review-skipped`), policy packs (`rules-migrate`) and the five `init-auto-*` cases.

## Cases

| Case | Fixture | Checks | Bare |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| investigate-how | ts-feature-boundary | note saved, citations valid, the answer names the service and route, decoys excluded | yes |
| investigate-files | ts-feature-boundary | the file list is the invoice boundary, not the keyword decoys | yes |
| investigate-nomatch | ts-feature-boundary | the scope gate is raised on an empty map, nothing invented | yes |
| plan-accept | ts-feature-boundary | six-field draft, valid anchors, promoted on Accept, no code touched | yes |
| investigate-trace | ts-app-medium | a payment flow that reaches notifications only through the event bus; the legacy hook is not part of it | yes |
| plan-reuse | ts-app-medium | the plan reuses shared validation, money and the reports module and leaves legacy alone | yes |
| plan-draft | ts-feature-boundary | with no answer the plan stays a draft and is not called accepted | no |
| task-fix | eval-page-bug | format, reviewer subagent, report sections, fix and test correct | yes |

Exit code 1

const CONFIG = '.ambicode/config.yaml';
const DRAFT_WRITE = String.raw`"file_path":"[^"]*\.ambicode/policies/drafts/[^"]*\.ya?ml"`;
// The scaffolded config keeps example entries in # comments (templates/config.yaml); a pattern must start on a line that is not one.
const LIVE = String.raw`(^|\n)[^#\n]*`;
const anyOf = (words) => `(${words.join('|')})`;

/** Deterministic graders first, one llm grader for the judgement no pattern carries. `b` is cases.mjs's builder set. */
export function initGraders(b, truth) {
  const { regex, tool, never, exists, llm } = b;
  const many = truth.projects.length > 1;
  const first = truth.projects[0];
  const graders = [
    tool('scaffold-ran', 'Bash', 'scaffold\\.mjs'),
    tool('scout-invoked', 'Agent', 'ambicode:scout'),
    tool('config-validated', 'Bash', 'config validate'),
    tool('config-packs-ran', 'Bash', 'config packs'),
    never('no-questions', 'AskUserQuestion', '.'),
    never('no-rules-route', 'Bash', 'route start rules'),
    exists('config-written', CONFIG),
    ...['overview', 'navigation', 'conventions', 'index'].map((name) => exists(`context-${name}`, `.ambicode/context/${name}.md`)),
    regex('gitignore-has-ambicode', String.raw`(^|\n)/?\.ambicode/?\s*(\n|$)`, { file: '.gitignore' }),
    regex('schema-version', `schemaVersion:\\s*${SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION}`, { file: CONFIG }),
    // Both forms: one project reads as a single `- id:` under projects, and a monorepo needs a second.
    regex(many ? 'projects-two-or-more' : 'projects-single', String.raw`\n\s*- id:[\s\S]*\n\s*- id:`, { file: CONFIG, match: many ? 'contains' : 'not_contains' }),
  ];
  for (const project of truth.projects) {
    const where = many ? `-${project.id}` : '';
    graders.push(
      regex(`ecosystem${where}`, `${LIVE}languages:[\\s\\S]{0,80}\\b${anyOf(project.languages.flatMap((l) => (l === 'kotlin' ? ['kotlin', 'java'] : [l])))}\\b`, { file: CONFIG }),
      regex(`root-or-paths${where}`, many ? `${LIVE}(root|paths):[\\s\\S]{0,40}${project.id}` : `${LIVE}paths:[\\s\\S]{0,40}${anyOf(project.paths.map((p) => p.replace(/\/$/, '')))}`, { file: CONFIG }),
      regex(`test-check${where}`, `${LIVE}(all|file):[^\\n]*(${project.checkPatterns.test})`, { file: CONFIG, weight: 2 }),
      regex(`lint-check${where}`, `${LIVE}(all|file):[^\\n]*(${project.checkPatterns.lint})`, { file: CONFIG }),
    );
    if (project.filePatterns.length > 0) {
      graders.push(regex(`file-placeholder${where}`, `${LIVE}file:[^\\n]*${anyOf(project.filePatterns)}[^\\n]*\\{file\\}`, { file: CONFIG }));
    }
  }
  // Rules are packs since config v5: init copies the built-ins it selects and writes no config rules.
  graders.push(
    exists('common-design-copied', packFile('builtin/common-design')),
    regex('policy-file-listed', 'policies/common/common-design\\.yaml', { file: CONFIG }),
    regex('no-misfit-pack', `builtin/${anyOf(truth.wrongPacks)}`, { file: CONFIG, match: 'not_contains' }),
    regex('no-config-rules', String.raw`source:\s*(scout|manual|web)|(^|\n)rules:|\n\s+instruction:`, { file: CONFIG, match: 'not_contains' }),
  );
  for (const pack of first.packs.filter((p) => !COMMON.includes(p) && truth.projects.length === 1)) graders.push(exists(`${pack.split('/')[1]}-copied`, packFile(pack)));
  if (truth.conventions.length > 0) {
    graders.push(tool('drafts-written', 'Write', DRAFT_WRITE));
    // --auto still drafts the scout's conventions (skills/init/SKILL.md step 5); it only skips the web search, the question and the rules route.
    for (const convention of truth.conventions) graders.push(tool(`draft-${convention.id}`, 'Write', `${DRAFT_WRITE}.*(${convention.draft})`));
  }
  const names = truth.projects.map((project) => project.id).join(', ');
  const wrong = truth.wrongPacks.map((p) => p.replace(/-$/, '')).join(', ');
  graders.push(llm('summary-and-pack-fit', `
PASS only if all hold:
- The final message names the project${many ? 's' : ''} found (expected: ${names}; ${truth.stack}) and the checks found for ${many ? 'each' : 'it'} (${truth.projects.map((p) => Object.keys(p.checkPatterns).join('/')).join(' and ')}), says which checks or commands are missing, and lists the context files written.
- It reports that config validate passed, or lists its errors; it does not claim success while showing errors.
- The policy packs it says were chosen fit the stack: the common-* packs are plausible anywhere${truth.projects.some((p) => p.packs.some((id) => !COMMON.includes(id))) ? `, and ${[...new Set(truth.projects.flatMap((p) => p.packs.filter((id) => !COMMON.includes(id))))].join(', ')} fit${truth.projects.length === 1 ? 's' : ''} the named project` : ''}. Any ${wrong} pack is a misfit.
FAIL otherwise.`));
  return graders;
}

export function initCases(b) {
  return INIT_TRUTHS.map((truth) => ({
    name: `init-auto-${truth.slug}`,
    description: `/ambicode:init --auto on an uninitialised repository: ${truth.stack}. Config, packs, context${truth.conventions.length > 0 ? ' and draft rules for three planted conventions' : ''}.`,
    tags: ['init'],
    version: truth.slug === 'ts' ? 5 : 1,
    fixture: truth.fixture, flags: truth.flags, intoCwd: true,
    prompt: '/ambicode:init --auto',
    bare: null,
    graders: initGraders(b, truth),
    files: { 'expected-config.yaml': expectedConfig(truth), 'truth.json': truthJson(truth) },
  }));
}

3	Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
4	Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens`, `context.maxIndexTokens` (`index.md` only) and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500, 5000 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).
5	
6	## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
7	- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
8	- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
9	- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
10	- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
