# Overview of parcelhub
## Purpose
- Parcel tracking for a regional courier: customers look up a parcel by tag, depot staff advance scan states.
- Depot staff also assign each parcel a sorting bay.
## Projects
- parcelhub - cmd, internal - Go daemon with JSON HTTP API
## Stack
- Go: language, standard module layout
- golangci-lint: linting
=== navigation.md
# Navigation of parcelhub
## How to read
- List the files, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset and limit; do not Read large files whole.
## Entry points
- cmd/parceld/main.go - HTTP daemon wiring all packages
## Where things live
- bay assignment: internal/depot
- HTTP handlers: internal/httpapi
- in-memory store: internal/memstore
- scan history and lookup: internal/tracking
- shared types and interfaces: internal/core
- system clock: internal/clock
## Naming
- One package per folder under internal, file named after the package.
## Grep patterns
- constructors: func New
=== conventions.md
# Conventions of parcelhub
## Code
- Shared interfaces (Store, Tracker, Clock) live in internal/core; implementations live in sibling packages.
- Each package exposes a New constructor.
- Only cmd/parceld wires packages together.
## Errors
## Tests
- Tests sit beside code as _test.go files.
## Imports
- Packages import internal/core for shared types.

---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself: it drops an extra path in a second, but it never finds a path you left out. When unsure, keep the path. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Match each entity to the deepest index line whose text names it or the feature it belongs to; a product or area name alone does not make its top-level line the match when a line below it fits better. Most ticket-related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <deepest index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 6 notes in total: the most specific ones, the deepest matching index lines from Stage A. Open a parent overview only when no line below it matches the ticket. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note keep every source the ticket changes, and every source that uses or is used by what it changes. A note line naming a path is evidence enough: it needs no Grep or Glob to count.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time. When an opened note's `## Submodules` names a child that matches a ticket term, open that child's note before a note from another part of the tree.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Keep same-kind siblings. When you keep one subfolder of a kind (one per item, field, variant or step), keep every sibling of that kind the note lists, unless the ticket excludes it.
   Example: the ticket renames the toggle label in every notification setting; `settings/` lists `email-row/`, `sms-row/`, `push-row/`, `profile/`. Answer all three `*-row/` folders, not only the one a Grep hit.
7. Drop only paths that are clearly unrelated to the ticket. When unsure, keep the path.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes. Every such folder goes into the answer, also outside the page or screen the ticket names; do not narrow the answer to one screen.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob only the paths you composed yourself, and drop one that does not exist; never guess a prefix. A path copied from a note line or a tool result exists: keep it without a Glob.

## Answer

Return every path you found related to the ticket, from the notes you read and from the Grep hits, with the dependencies the change reaches. A note line or a Grep hit is the evidence; a path needs no other confirmation. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. Paths are relative to the repository root: never copy the absolute working-directory part of a path a tool printed or you passed to it. 5. Switch model to haiku after 1-3. Cost effect unmeasured (haiku price unknown; I'd guess about half per token, unverified). Gate it with the proposed graders on 15 runs.

- Haiku price and behaviour; main-session cost for inseer inits (so "78%" cannot be confirmed; fixtures show 43%).

- The 5 inseer scout runs without jsonl; `tool_used` seeing subagent calls; `context tree` with no `--root`.
- Inseer tree count at final-write time.

content.text: Logged.

Главное из исследования: на маленьких fixture scout дешёвый, а дорогим он становится на большом репозитории. Мои прошлые 78% неверны. Если пересчитать по токенам, scout занимает 43% стоимости прогона на fixture. Тот 78% брался из `breakdown.mjs`, и откуда расхождение между двумя расчётами, я пока не выяснил.

```
                     turns   $/scout run   context at end
fixtures (15 runs)   6-8     .059-.108     17-21k
inseer, 13 turns     8-13    .30-.57       48-84k
inseer, 56 turns     56      2.33          179k   (custom prompt, 32 ad-hoc Bash)
```

**Куда уходят деньги на inseer-frontend**
- Около трети, а иногда половину, съедает текст, который scout пишет в файлы контекста (bundles). Файлы overview, navigation и conventions он переписывает на каждом уровне, и это 7–42% этого текста.
- 17–28% уходит на результаты `context tree` и `--level`. Полное дерево занимает около 6k токенов и потом пересылается на каждом следующем ходу.
- `--index` модель просто копирует из вывода в `context write`, хотя это механика. Это стоит лишних 1–2 хода.
- На fixture больше половины стоимости дают системный промпт и чтение `context-format.md` (7.7 KB).
- 11 из 44 записей контекста отклонила его собственная проверка (`check.problems`), из-за чего их пришлось повторять.

**Качество**
- Покрытие модулей полное, но это заслуга CLI: он сам выдаёт scout список модулей.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` scout не прочитал ни разу (0 из 9 прогонов python/go/jvm). Из заложенных конвенций найдено 6 из 24 записанных в документации и 0 из 12 видимых только в коде.
- Черновики rules не появляются по вине основной сессии, а не scout: монорепо получил от scout 2 правила, и основная сессия их не записала.

**Рычаги, по убыванию эффекта**
1. **CLI.** Все уровни дерева выдавать одним вызовом, а `context write` пусть сам строит index. Ожидаю −20–30% ходов и стоимости на большом репо и минус два шага, на которых haiku может споткнуться. Это правка существующего кода.
2. **Промпт.** Overview, navigation и conventions писать один раз, а не на каждом уровне.
3. **Промпт.** Сократить его и `context-format.md`, убрать шаги, которые модель всё равно не выполняет (Grep/Glob не вызывался ни разу).
4. **Промпт.** Читать contributor-доки. Это даст качество ценой +1 Read.
5. **Haiku.** Переключаться после пунктов 1–3. Цену прогона на haiku я не измерял.

**Нужно ваше решение: на чём мерить стоимость.** Fixture содержат 1–5 модулей, поэтому рычаги 1–3 на них почти не проявятся. Предлагаю так:
- **Fixture оставить для качества.** Добавлю грейдеры scout, которые предложил субагент: заметки по модулям существуют, index на них ссылается, CONTRIBUTING прочитан, в `conventions.md` нет must/never, заложенные конвенции находятся. Это закрывает p1, $0.
- **Стоимость мерить отдельным прогоном только scout на inseer-frontend** с записью в отдельную папку, бэкап не трогаю. На sonnet это около $0.4 за прогон, ×3 даёт примерно **$1.2–1.5** как базовую линию до правок.

Подойдёт такой подход? Или вместо inseer сделать синтетическую fixture покрупнее, на 40–60 модулей? Тогда замер будет воспроизводимым, но ещё один пункт на поддержку.

135	      id: project.id,
136	      root: project.root,
137	      paths: project.paths,
138	      ecosystem: { languages: project.languages, frameworks: project.frameworks, packageManager: project.packageManager },

140	      exclude: project.exclude,
141	      ignored: [],
142	      packs: project.packs,

144	      commands: {},

151	  stack: truth.stack,
152	  projects: truth.projects.map(({ id, root, paths, languages, packs, checks }) => ({ id, root, paths, languages, packs, checks })),
153	  plausiblePacks: [...new Set(truth.projects.flatMap((project) => project.packs))],
154	  packsThatDoNotFit: truth.wrongPacks,
155	  conventions: truth.conventions.map(({ id, basis, quote, location, document }) => ({ id, basis, quote, location, ...(document ? { document } : {}) })),
156	}, null, 2)}\n`;

158	const CONFIG = '.ambicode/config.yaml';
159	const DRAFT_WRITE = String.raw`"file_path":"[^"]*\.ambicode/policies/drafts/[^"]*\.ya?ml"`;
160	// The scaffolded config keeps example entries in # comments (templates/config.yaml); a pattern must start on a line that is not one.
161	const LIVE = String.raw`(^|\n)[^#\n]*`;
162	const anyOf = (words) => `(${words.join('|')})`;

164	/** Deterministic graders first, one llm grader for the judgement no pattern carries. `b` is cases.mjs's builder set. */
165	export function initGraders(b, truth) {
166	  const { regex, tool, never, exists, llm } = b;
167	  const many = truth.projects.length > 1;
168	  const first = truth.projects[0];
169	  const graders = [
170	    tool('scaffold-ran', 'Bash', 'scaffold\\.mjs'),
171	    tool('scout-invoked', 'Agent', 'ambicode:scout'),
172	    tool('config-validated', 'Bash', 'config validate'),
173	    tool('config-packs-ran', 'Bash', 'config packs'),
174	    never('no-questions', 'AskUserQuestion', '.'),
175	    never('no-rules-route', 'Bash', 'route start rules'),
176	    exists('config-written', CONFIG),
177	    ...['overview', 'navigation', 'conventions', 'index'].map((name) => exists(`context-${name}`, `.ambicode/context/${name}.md`)),
178	    regex('gitignore-has-ambicode', String.raw`(^|\n)/?\.ambicode/?\s*(\n|$)`, { file: '.gitignore' }),
179	    regex('schema-version', `schemaVersion:\\s*${SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION}`, { file: CONFIG }),
180	    // Both forms: one project reads as a single `- id:` under projects, and a monorepo needs a second.
181	    regex(many ? 'projects-two-or-more' : 'projects-single', String.raw`\n\s*- id:[\s\S]*\n\s*- id:`, { file: CONFIG, match: many ? 'contains' : 'not_contains' }),
182	  ];
183	  for (const project of truth.projects) {
184	    const where = many ? `-${project.id}` : '';
185	    graders.push(
186	      regex(`ecosystem${where}`, `${LIVE}languages:[\\s\\S]{0,80}\\b${anyOf(project.languages.flatMap((l) => (l === 'kotlin' ? ['kotlin', 'java'] : [l])))}\\b`, { file: CONFIG }),
187	      regex(`root-or-paths${where}`, many ? `${LIVE}(root|paths):[\\s\\S]{0,40}${project.id}` : `${LIVE}paths:[\\s\\S]{0,40}${anyOf(project.paths.map((p) => p.replace(/\/$/, '')))}`, { file: CONFIG }),
188	      regex(`test-check${where}`, `${LIVE}(all|file):[^\\n]*(${project.checkPatterns.test})`, { file: CONFIG, weight: 2 }),
189	      regex(`lint-check${where}`, `${LIVE}(all|file):[^\\n]*(${project.checkPatterns.lint})`, { file: CONFIG }),
190	    );
191	    if (project.filePatterns.length > 0) {
192	      graders.push(regex(`file-placeholder${where}`, `${LIVE}file:[^\\n]*${anyOf(project.filePatterns)}[^\\n]*\\{file\\}`, { file: CONFIG }));
193	    }
194	  }
195	  // Rules are packs since config v5: init copies the built-ins it selects and writes no config rules.
196	  graders.push(
197	    exists('common-design-copied', packFile('builtin/common-design')),
198	    regex('policy-file-listed', 'policies/common/common-design\\.yaml', { file: CONFIG }),
199	    regex('no-misfit-pack', `builtin/${anyOf(truth.wrongPacks)}`, { file: CONFIG, match: 'not_contains' }),
200	    regex('no-config-rules', String.raw`source:\s*(scout|manual|web)|(^|\n)rules:|\n\s+instruction:`, { file: CONFIG, match: 'not_contains' }),
201	  );
202	  for (const pack of first.packs.filter((p) => !COMMON.includes(p) && truth.projects.length === 1)) graders.push(exists(`${pack.split('/')[1]}-copied`, packFile(pack)));
203	  if (truth.conventions.length > 0) {
204	    graders.push(tool('drafts-written', 'Write', DRAFT_WRITE));
205	    // --auto still drafts the scout's conventions (skills/init/SKILL.md step 5); it only skips the web search, the question and the rules route.
206	    for (const convention of truth.conventions) graders.push(tool(`draft-${convention.id}`, 'Write', `${DRAFT_WRITE}.*(${convention.draft})`));
207	  }
208	  const names = truth.projects.map((project) => project.id).join(', ');
209	  const wrong = truth.wrongPacks.map((p) => p.replace(/-$/, '')).join(', ');
210	  graders.push(llm('summary-and-pack-fit', `
211	PASS only if all hold:
212	- The final message names the project${many ? 's' : ''} found (expected: ${names}; ${truth.stack}) and the checks found for ${many ? 'each' : 'it'} (${truth.projects.map((p) => Object.keys(p.checkPatterns).join('/')).join(' and ')}), says which checks or commands are missing, and lists the context files written.
213	- It reports that config validate passed, or lists its errors; it does not claim success while showing errors.
214	- The policy packs it says were chosen fit the stack: the common-* packs are plausible anywhere${truth.projects.some((p) => p.packs.some((id) => !COMMON.includes(id))) ? `, and ${[...new Set(truth.projects.flatMap((p) => p.packs.filter((id) => !COMMON.includes(id))))].join(', ')} fit${truth.projects.length === 1 ? 's' : ''} the named project` : ''}. Any ${wrong} pack is a misfit.
215	FAIL otherwise.`));
216	  return graders;
217	}

855	    "        log.atInfo().addKeyValue(\"lotId\", id.value).addKeyValue(\"trays\", trays).log(\"lot.sown\")",

1202	    "",
1203	    "#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]",
1204	    "pub enum SafetyError {",
1205	    "    Empty,",
1206	    "    TooHot { target_dc: i32 },",
1207	    "    TooCold { target_dc: i32 },",
1208	    "}",
1209	    "",
1210	    "pub fn check_setpoint_dc(target_dc: i32) -> Result<(), SafetyError> {",
1211	    "    if target_dc > MAX_SETPOINT_DC {",
1212	    "        return Err(SafetyError::TooHot { target_dc });",
1213	    "    }",
1214	    "    if target_dc < MIN_SETPOINT_DC {",
1215	    "        return Err(SafetyError::TooCold { target_dc });",
1216	    "    }",

1222	    "",
1223	    "#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]",
1224	    "pub struct Segment {",
1225	    "    pub minutes: u32,",
1226	    "    pub target_dc: i32,",
1227	    "}",
1228	    "",
1229	    "#[derive(Debug, Clone)]",
1230	    "pub struct Schedule {",
1231	    "    segments: Vec<Segment>,",
1232	    "}",
1233	    "",
1234	    "impl Schedule {",
1235	    "    pub fn new(segments: Vec<Segment>) -> Result<Self, SafetyError> {",
1236	    "        if segments.is_empty() {",
1237	    "            return Err(SafetyError::Empty);",
1238	    "        }",
1239	    "        for segment in &segments {",
1240	    "            check_setpoint_dc(segment.target_dc)?;",
1241	    "        }",
1242	    "        Ok(Self { segments })",
1243	    "    }",
1244	    "",
1245	    "    pub fn total_minutes(&self) -> u32 {",
1246	    "        self.segments.iter().map(|segment| segment.minutes).sum()",
1247	    "    }",
1248	    "",
1249	    "    pub fn target_at_dc(&self, minute: u32) -> i32 {",
1250	    "        let mut elapsed = 0;",
1251	    "        for segment in &self.segments {",
1252	    "            elapsed += segment.minutes;",
1253	    "            if minute < elapsed {",
1254	    "                return segment.target_dc;",
1255	    "            }",
1256	    "        }",
1257	    "        self.segments",
1258	    "            .last()",
1259	    "            .map(|segment| segment.target_dc)",
1260	    "            .expect(\"invariant: Schedule::new rejects an empty segment list\")",
1261	    "    }",
1262	    "}",

# Evals: skill coverage

Twenty-one synthetic cases, at least one per skill, each checking one behaviour. Twelve of them also run with no
plugin loaded, which is the baseline. Every case runs on a fixture from `fixtures/definitions.mjs`, so nothing
here is real project data and the whole suite is in git. The previous benchmark suites are in `archive/evals/`
and are not run any more.

```
evals/
  scripts/cases.mjs       the single source: every case, its prompt per arm, its graders
  cases/<case>/           plugin arm, generated (claude plugin eval layout: case.yaml, prompt.md, scaffold.sh, graders/)
  bare/<case>/            no-plugin arm, generated: same request in plain words, shared graders only
  scripts/run.mjs         runs one arm through `claude plugin eval` and leaves the result in `cases/results/`
  scripts/context.mjs     reads context size, session and model seconds, and session cost from each run's trace
  scripts/trace.mjs       trace parsing and `mean`, shared by the scripts below
  scripts/metrics.mjs     recall, precision and F1 of the files an answer lists (cases that declare `metrics`)
  scripts/breakdown.mjs   where a run's calls, tokens, seconds and injected bytes go (`npm run evals:breakdown -- <trace.jsonl | dir>`)
  cases/results/          raw output of the last run per arm, and traces/<arm>/<stamp>/<case>-<n>.jsonl with the run's ledgers in `.ambicode` beside it, `context/` included (gitignored)
```

## Run

```sh
npm run build                       # cases run scripts/ambicode.mjs, not src/
npm run evals                       # plugin arm: 21 cases
npm run evals:bare                  # bare arm: 12 cases, no plugin
npm run evals -- --case 'task-*'    # one skill (a glob; --case is not repeatable)
npm run evals -- --tag gate         # by tag
npm run evals -- --runs 3           # more runs per case, for a decision
npm run evals:dry                   # print both commands and change nothing
```

Defaults: Sonnet 5.5, effort low, 1 run per case, 4 runs in parallel, a $15 cap per arm. Override any of them with
`--model`, `--effort`, `--runs` or `--max-cost-usd`. The harness has no effort flag, so `run.mjs` sets
`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` in the environment. A probe showed the variable inside the run. It does not prove the
model honoured it.

Read a run in `evals/cases/results/<arm>.json` and its traces under `results/traces/<arm>/<run time>/`; the plugin-master viewer shows both.

## Navigator cases

Ten ordinary cases (`fe-vs-<id>-navigator`; the asset folders keep their `fe-vs-<id>-investigate` names) on the NDA bench repo in `../ambicode-evals-assets`, rendered by
`scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (also run by `npm run evals:generate`) into `evals/cases/navigator/` (plugin arm) and
`evals/bare/navigator/` (bare arm). Both are gitignored: they hold ticket text and truth paths. Without the assets the generator
prints one line and skips; env `NAV_BENCH`, `NAV_CASES` override the sibling-directory defaults.

```sh
npm run evals -- --tag navigator        # plugin arm, one harness call, -j 4
npm run evals:bare -- --tag navigator   # bare arm
```

- Each run starts with the bench copied into a fresh git repo and no `.ambicode/`. The plugin arm's scaffold copies the
  bench's `.ambicode/context/` back in, because the navigator reads only that; the bare scaffold copies nothing.
- The prompt is the ticket plus one instruction, the same for both arms: return the files as a ```files block. The plugin arm
  measures the navigator alone: `allowed_tools: [Agent]`, no `--allow-tools` shell grant, and an `append_system_prompt` that makes
  the session call `ambicode:navigator` once in the foreground and copy its paths unchanged (grader `navigator-called`). The harness
  has no main-agent option, and its tool lists bind subagents too, so the session keeps the read tools; the relay text forbids using them.
- Score = recall over the truth folders. The nav truth (logic files; i18n and fixtures dropped; companion files dropped except that a companion-only directory becomes a directory item) is collapsed to its unique folders, and a folder is covered when any line of the first ```files block is that folder, lies under it, or is an ancestor directory (or a file directly in one) with at least 30% of the source folders under it covered by the truth (`ancestors` in `truth.json`, computed from the bench at generation; the 0.3 is a choice, not measured). One regex grader per truth folder. Step graders (`files-block`, plugin-only `navigator-called`) weigh 0.0001 each, so
  score = (hits + 0.0001 * steps passed) / (|T| + 0.0001 * steps) is within 1e-4 of recall. Precision and F1 come from
  `truth.json` in the case dir (nav truth `relevant`, the rest `allowed`, plus `level: 'folder'`, `ancestorShare` and the `ancestors` map, which the graders and `scoreNavigator` read). `run.mjs` writes `recall`, `precision`, `f1`, `missed`, `extra` and `contract` into each run's `metrics` in the result JSON, computed by `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` from the trace's first ```files block and `truth.json`. Recall is pinned to the recall graders (passed / total); if the computed value differs, the grader value is written and `mismatch: true` is set.
- `--tag navigator` is one `claude plugin eval` call at the default `-j 4`, like any other selection: the cases share no state.
  The result goes to `cases/results/<arm>.json` and, with the metrics, to `cases/results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`
  (bare: `cases/results/bare/<stamp>/`), which the viewer reads.
- Navigator cases run only with `--tag navigator`: an unfiltered run lists the skill tags instead (the harness has no exclude option).


## Recall, precision, drift

A case with `metrics` in `cases.mjs` is scored on the files its answer lists. The prompt asks both arms for a
`## Files` section, and only that section counts, because answers also name decoys in order to rule them out.
- **Recall** is the share of the `relevant` files the list names.
- **Precision** is the share of listed files that are `relevant` or `allowed`.
- **F1** combines the two.
- Navigator cases do not use `scoreFiles` (it stays file-level, for the skill cases). `scoreNavigator` in `navigator-cases.mjs` computes recall, precision and F1 by the folder rule and `run.mjs` writes them to the result JSON; a viewer reads them generically from `metrics`. The rule: a file counts as its directory, a truth folder is covered by an answer folder equal to or under it, or above it when at least 30% of the source folders under that ancestor (directories holding a logic file) are covered; an answer folder is correct when related the same way to a folder of `relevant` or `allowed`.

A run with no Files section scores recall 0 and F1 0, and is counted separately.

Read the result files, not the exit code. The harness exits 1 whenever any case scores below 1.0.

## How a case works

1. **Scaffold.** `scaffold.sh` replays a fixture into `repo/`, a fresh git repository with known history. The
   plugin arm also commits `.ambicode/config.yaml`. `--install` fixtures run `npm ci`, so jest and eslint are real. `--context` also writes
   `fixtures/contexts/<fixture>.md` into the gitignored `.ambicode/context`, standing in for the scout (8 of the 21 cases).
2. **Prompt.** The plugin arm types the skill exactly as a user would, for example
   `/ambicode:task --task fix-page --headless --answer review-offer=run Fix page() …`. `--task` fixes the slug so
   graders can find the ledger. `--answer` pre-answers a gate. A case with no answer tests the gate's default. The
   bare arm sends the same request in plain words: "Fix page() …", or "Review the uncommitted change in `repo/`".
3. **Graders.** They run after the session ends, on what it left behind:
   - `regex` on the ledger (`repo/.ambicode/tasks/<slug>/ledger.jsonl`), on a produced file, or on the final message.
   - `tool_used` on the trace, for example the `Agent` tool with `ambicode:reviewer`, or "never `git commit`".
   - `file_exists` for files the run created.
   - `llm` when only judgment works: is the answer right, is the fix right, is the gap stated. Haiku judges with
     three votes.
4. **Score.** The weighted share of graders that passed.

## Plugin against bare

Graders come in two kinds:

- **Shared graders** judge the outcome: the answer, the code, the review finding, the boundary (no edits, no git).
  They run in both arms.
- **Plugin-only graders** check what only AMBICODE writes: ledger entries, the reviewer subagent, report sections.
  They run in the plugin arm only.

Nine cases have no bare arm because what they test belongs to the plugin: a gate default (`plan-draft`,
`task-review-skipped`, `review-skipped`), policy packs (`rules-migrate`) and the five `init-auto-*` cases.

## Cases

| Case | Fixture | Checks | Bare |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| investigate-how | ts-feature-boundary | note saved, citations valid, the answer names the service and route, decoys excluded | yes |
| investigate-files | ts-feature-boundary | the file list is the invoice boundary, not the keyword decoys | yes |
| investigate-nomatch | ts-feature-boundary | the scope gate is raised on an empty map, nothing invented | yes |
| plan-accept | ts-feature-boundary | six-field draft, valid anchors, promoted on Accept, no code touched | yes |
| investigate-trace | ts-app-medium | a payment flow that reaches notifications only through the event bus; the legacy hook is not part of it | yes |
| plan-reuse | ts-app-medium | the plan reuses shared validation, money and the reports module and leaves legacy alone | yes |
| plan-draft | ts-feature-boundary | with no answer the plan stays a draft and is not called accepted | no |
| task-fix | eval-page-bug | format, reviewer subagent, report sections, fix and test correct | yes |
| task-multi | ts-app-medium-refund-bug | a fix across payments service and repository with AppError and the test factory | yes |
| task-review-skipped | eval-page-bug | the review offer defaults to skip and the report says so | no |
| review-defect | ts-off-by-one | the off-by-one is found with its location | yes |
| review-subtle | ts-app-medium-money-change | the broken caller outside the diff is named, the bare Error is flagged | yes |
| review-clean | py-clean-docstring | no false defect, verification gap stated | yes |
| review-regression | ts-source-regression | a check is recorded, the broken behaviour is found | yes |
| review-skipped | ts-off-by-one | the estimate gate defaults to skip, no reviewer, no finding | no |
| rules-migrate | eval-rules-contributing | drafts checked and applied, the vague line and the embedded `rm -rf` ignored | no |
| init-auto-ts | ts-feature-boundary, no config, jest and eslint installed | scaffold, scout subagent, context files, checks wired, packs copied, config validated | no |
| init-auto-python | py-service-tidewatch | as above on pytest and ruff, plus draft rules for three planted conventions (TW- error codes, `test_<module>__<behaviour>` names, keyword-only arguments) | no |
| init-auto-go | go-module-parcelhub | go test, go vet, golangci-lint; drafts for `pkg.Func: %w` wrapping, an injected Clock, imports through `internal/core` | no |
| init-auto-jvm | jvm-gradle-seedvault | Kotlin on Gradle; drafts for value-class ids, `Outcome` instead of exceptions, structured log key-values | no |
| init-auto-monorepo | monorepo-rust-ts-kiln | two projects (Rust `engine/`, Express `dashboard/`); drafts for `_dc` units, `expect("invariant: ...")`, `register(app)` route modules | no |

The init cases share their graders (`evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs`); each case directory also holds `expected-config.yaml` and `truth.json`, the result init should reach and the planted conventions with quotes. Written conventions sit in the fixture's CONTRIBUTING.md, inferred ones only in code. `node evals/scripts/cases.mjs --case 'init-*'` rewrites just these cases and leaves the navigator cases alone. `init-cases.test.mjs` checks them at no cost; no paid run has scored them yet.

## Change or add a case

1. Edit `evals/scripts/cases.mjs`. Use an existing fixture or add an `eval-*` one to `fixtures/definitions.mjs`.
   Wrap a grader in `shared(...)` when a bare run could pass it too. Pass a second grader when the bare arm reads
   the artefact somewhere else, like `plan-quality`, which reads the plan file in one arm and the message in the
   other.
2. `npm run evals:generate`. It rewrites `evals/cases/` and `evals/bare/`, so never edit those by hand.
   `suite.test.mjs` fails when the trees drift from `cases.mjs`.
3. `node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs`, then `npm run evals -- --case <name>` and, if it has a bare arm,
   `npm run evals:bare -- --case <name>`.

Keep a case to one behaviour and under 15 graders. Ledger entry shapes are in `src/platform/ledger/kinds.ts`. Graders
must name literal paths, because the harness does not resolve globs.

---
name: implementer
description: AMBICODE's implementer. Carries out one work brief (a work file with the rules, the findings to fix and the runnable checks) and records the green check. Invoked only by the task route; never by a natural-language request.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash
model: sonnet
---

# Implementer role

The request names one work file: read it first. It holds the brief, the search map, the project
rules, the runnable checks and the exact `check` command to run. Do what it says, no more.
The work file is complete: do not read the ledger or any other file under `.ambicode/tasks/`.

## Rules

- Make the smallest change the brief needs. Reuse existing code before adding.
- Never weaken or delete a test to pass. Add or update tests with the project's helpers.
- Run tests only through the `check` command in the work file, and record each run. Fix and re-run
  until it is green.
- Edit only: never commit, push or publish, never run git commands that change state, never edit
  `.ambicode/`.
- If a check needs the user's approval, or you cannot reach green, stop and say so.

## Finish

The green check is your last tool call. Your final message is exactly:

```
Changed:
- path:line — what and why (path relative to the repository root, never absolute)
Checks: <check name>: <result>, ...
Gaps: none
```

One `Changed:` line per changed file. `Gaps:` lists what is not done or not verified, or `none`.
---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself: it drops an extra path in a second, but it never finds a path you left out. When unsure, keep the path. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Match each entity to the deepest index line whose text names it or the feature it belongs to; a product or area name alone does not make its top-level line the match when a line below it fits better. Most ticket-related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <deepest index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

---
name: scout
description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---
You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Follow this recipe exactly.

Walk the tree breadth-first: all folders of one level before any deeper. Visit each directory at most once in the whole run: keep a running list of visited directories and move on to one not on it. Locate names and files with Grep and Glob first; read content only when search results do not settle a module's purpose.

Never read a file whole (except the format spec in step 1): only heads or ranges with a line limit. Never read styles, tests or specs, mocks or fixtures, stories, nor generated, vendored, lock or build files.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only as heads with limit <= 40, only non-excluded ones, and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names and search. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language string catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms.
5. Level info, once per level before you write it: Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --level <n>` (the same roots as step 3; the roots' modules are level 1). It prints, for every folder of that level, a linked folder line and one line per unique file base name (the file name without the suffixes after its first dot) with the entity names its files declare; tests, stories, mocks, styles and templates are left out. Use it for each folder's purpose together with the heads you read.
6. Write level by level. After you have gathered one breadth-first level, write that level's notes, plus `overview.md` and `navigation.md` updated for everything seen so far (never `index.md` here), then go to the next level. Each write is one call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec and the same roots as step 3. The first write adds `--replace`; later writes omit it, so they add or update only the files in their bundle and keep the rest. `index.md` links may name only notes already written or in that bundle. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: fix those notes from what you just read and write that level again before going deeper. Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

`## Purpose` has 2 bullets of at most 25 words each: the first says what the folder is for in the product's own words (the titles and abbreviations read in step 4, the entity names from step 5), the second says what roles it contains (the kinds of things its subfolders and base names are); neither restates the folder name or says "source files of ... scope". Write `## Key files` and `## Folders` as empty headings: `context write` fills them from the code, and it generates the `Root:` field, so write paths relative to the module directory or none. To describe a file, repeat its generated bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares; to describe a folded folder, repeat its generated bullet as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>`. Each description is at most 12 words and comes from the names and level info only, with no extra file reads.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>` (the full note path is accepted: `context write` makes it relative), so a reader can find it from the parent. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

`index.md` is the folder tree the spec describes: its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, and where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Build it from the output of Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --index` (the same roots): it prints the whole `index.md` body within the `context.maxIndexTokens` budget: one line per module folder with the first Purpose bullet of its note and the names of its Key files, shallowest levels first, so every note it links must already be written. Copy it as printed and add nothing else. Run it only after the last level's notes are written, then write `index.md` alone in one more `context write` call (no `--replace`), so every description is read from a written note.

Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is for the commands in steps 2, 3 and 5 (`git ls-files`, `context tree` with and without `--level` or `--index`), the `context write` in step 6, and plain read-only listing (`ls`, `git ls-files`). Use Glob for file lookup.

Final message (returned to the caller, not written to disk), compact:
- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).

160:    name: 'ts-feature-boundary',
# Context format (`.ambicode/context/`)

Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens`, `context.maxIndexTokens` (`index.md` only) and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500, 5000 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).

## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
- `index.md`: the grep target for ticket words, one file, see below.

## Per-file structure
- H1 = the file's purpose, one line, unique across all files. Exactly one H1.
- H2 sections fixed per kind, in this order, each heading at most once per file. Keep an empty section's heading, omit its bullets.
  - `overview.md`: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Projects` (`- <id> - <path> - <what it is>`), `## Stack` (`- <tool>: <role>`).
  - `navigation.md`: `## How to read` (one bullet: list, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset/limit; never Read whole large files), `## Entry points` (`- <path> - <role>`), `## Where things live` (`- <thing>: <path or glob>`), `## Naming`, `## Grep patterns` (`- <what>: <pattern>`).
  - `conventions.md`: `## Code`, `## Errors`, `## Tests`, `## Imports`; one convention per bullet.
  - module notes: `Root: <module dir from the repo root>` directly under the H1 (generated by `context write`; never write it; every other path in the note is relative to it), `## Purpose` (2 bullets: what the folder is for, then what roles it contains), `## Key files` (filled by `context write` from the code: `- <path relative to Root> - <Name>, <Name>, ...` per source file of the module itself, files with the most exported declarations first, within the file limit; do not write it, only a bullet that repeats a generated path as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` is kept), `## Folders` (filled by `context write`; write only the empty heading: the folders below the module that hold source files but are not modules, one bullet each, `- <dir relative to Root>/ - <base name>, <base name>, ...`, so every source folder is named in some note; a bullet repeated as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>` is kept), `## Submodules` (`- <child note path relative to this note's directory> - <what that folder holds>`, e.g. from `modules/a/b/overview.md` the child `modules/a/b/c.md` is `c.md` and `modules/a/b/c/overview.md` is `c/overview.md`; `context write` rewrites a full `modules/...` path to this form and reports `submodule-link` for one that names no note; only for a module that has child modules), `## Depends on`, `## Gotchas`.
- `index.md`: H1, then the folder tree of the modules, nothing else. One line per module folder, indented two spaces per tree level (roots are level 1), as a link to that folder's note: `- [<dir>](<note path>)`, where the link text is the folder path relative to the folder line above it (a root folder keeps its full path) and the link target is always the full note path; the full folder path is the target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`. Each line may end with ` - <description>`: the first `## Purpose` bullet of that folder's note, cut at 12 words, and then ` | <Name>, <Name>, ...`: the names of that note's `## Key files` bullets without their paths, deduplicated, the first 8 then `+N` (both generated from the notes on disk; a folder whose note is missing or lacks the section has no such part; names without a description give `- [<dir>](<note path>) | <names>`). A child folder's line follows its parent's line. There are no file lines: files and entities are in the notes' `## Key files` and `## Folders`. Every link must name a note of the bundle or already written. Folders are listed level by level, parents before children, shallowest first, up to the last whole level that fits the budget; deeper folders are reached through the parent note's `## Submodules` links. No other lines: no aliases, no categories, no invented names. It has its own budget, `context.maxIndexTokens` (default 5000, not `maxFileTokens`) and counts toward `maxTotalTokens`. Its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. `ambicode context tree --level <n>` prints a level with its file lines for the scout; those lines are not index.md lines. Example:

  ```
  # Index
  - [src/billing](modules/src/billing/overview.md) - Invoices, tax and payment export | Invoice, InvoiceLine, totalOf, taxFor
    - [export](modules/src/billing/export.md) - CSV and PDF export of invoices | writeCsv, renderPdf
  - [src/auth](modules/src/auth.md) - Sign-in and session handling | Session, startSession
  ```
- Bullets sorted by path or name. Same repo state gives the same file.
- No hedging ("probably", "seems"), no dates, no drifting counts.
- No code bodies: code fences are refused; a signature is one line inside a bullet. Paths over prose.
- One fact in one file; point to another by relative path.

## Bundle format for `context write`
One call, bundle on stdin; each file starts with a line `=== <path relative to .ambicode/context/>`:

```
=== overview.md
# Overview of <repo>
## Purpose
- ...
=== modules/<note path from context tree>
# <directory> module
...
```

- `ambicode context write --replace` removes context files not in the bundle; without `--replace` only the named files change. `--root <dir>` (repeatable, the roots of `context tree`) tells it which module tree decides which module a file belongs to.
- Output is JSON `{written, removed, check: {problems}}`. Exit 1 and nothing written when `problems` is not empty (file too large, total too large, bad index.md line or indentation, index link to a missing note, duplicate H2 in a file, duplicate H1 across files, code fence, path outside the kinds). Fix with one more call naming only the changed files.
- `ambicode context list` prints path, H1 and approximate tokens per file, indented by folder; notes more than two levels down are counted on their level-1 parent.
- `ambicode context tree [--root <dir>...]` prints the modules of the source roots at full depth (note path, directory, depth, file count, submodules); it writes nothing.
- `ambicode context tree --root <dir> --index` prints the index.md body described above, built from the notes already written.
- `ambicode context tree --root <dir> --level <n>` prints one level of that tree in the index.md shape: each folder of the level (roots are level 1) as a linked line, then one line per unique file base name with the names its files declare. Companions (tests, stories, mocks, styles, templates) are left out. Names beyond 8 per base name are counted as `+N`.

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any


class Bus:
    def __init__(self) -> None:

class JournalStore:

input.message:
Commit 7b7ed5df "init: scout model and effort from config". `npm run verify` exits 0 (1253 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, 1 todo). The todo is `review-route.test.ts` 08-R5, which I did not touch. Whether the Agent call really receives haiku is unverified: no real run was done.

**Precedence.** I read the strings of the installed `claude` binary (~/.local/bin/claude). No docs on disk covered this.
- Subagent model is resolved by `JB`/`vms`; the telemetry in `vms` names the order: `tool` (the Agent `model` param, enum sonnet/opus/haiku/fable) > `frontmatter` > `env` (`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, `gse()`) > inherit.
- `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` discards the tool param and frontmatter (`ozt`) and uses only the env var. `run.mjs` stripping `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL*` therefore means neither the env var nor FORCE can interfere in evals.
- The frontmatter `model: sonnet` in `agents/scout.md` therefore loses to a passed `model`. It is only the fallback when the skill passes nothing. I left it.
- Effort: the Agent tool has an `effort` param. Its description says to set it only when a skill or CLAUDE.md asks for it, which `init` does. The `effort_param` telemetry shows it is read per call. I did not find an effort frontmatter field for plugin agents.
- The navigator hard-codes `model: haiku` in frontmatter with no config seam, so there was nothing to reuse.

**Mechanism chosen.** The scaffold prints the resolved settings, so step 2 copies exact values instead of reading YAML by eye.
- `config validate --json` already parses the config with zod. Its data now includes `scout: {model, effort}` when the config is valid.
- `scaffold.mjs` runs `config validate --json` through the CLI path it already uses for `init record`, and adds `scout` to its JSON. `scout` is absent if the config is invalid or the CLI is missing.
- `SKILL.md` step 2 now reads: "Launch `ambicode:scout` ... (`model`, `effort` from scaffold `scout`; omit if absent)". I dropped the "Read config.yaml" instruction. The init body stays under its 1,536-byte test cap. I shortened my wording rather than raise the cap.
- Haiku is not hard-coded anywhere. The default stays sonnet/medium from `templates/config.yaml`.

**Rejected.**
- (b) `model: inherit` or removing the frontmatter model: not needed, because the passed value already wins. It would also change the fallback away from sonnet.
- A new `config scout` CLI command: the existing `validate` command already parses the config.
- Parsing YAML inside `scaffold.mjs`: it has no yaml dependency, and a regex on the flow-style line breaks when the user edits the config.

**Files changed.**
- `skills/init/SKILL.md`
- `skills/init/scripts/scaffold.mjs`
- `src/cli/commands/config/validate.ts`
- `src/skills/init/scripts.test.ts`

**Tests.**
- A new test runs the scaffold against the real CLI (`src/cli/main.ts`). It expects `{sonnet, medium}` by default, `{haiku, low}` after a config override, and no `scout` for an invalid config.
- I updated the existing `--task` test, whose fake CLI now sees a second call, `config|validate|--json`.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass, including route validation and the `validate:plugin` step.
- The skill-content, init-trail and scripts tests pass.

**Unverified.**
- That the model, when following SKILL.md, passes both `model` and `effort` on the Agent call. The prior traces showed `model: "sonnet"` passed and effort not visible.
- That `haiku` as a config value is accepted by the Agent tool's `model` enum. `Name` is free-form, so a value outside sonnet/opus/haiku/fable would be rejected at call time.
- Precedence comes from reading binary strings, not from a live call.

Another agent's files were not touched, and `.plugin-master/` was not committed.

## Current version

0.6.1 (bumped in 33c2a5b4 after p12 cleanup; `npm run verify` green 2026-10-20, 1236 tests 0 fail). Branch `navigator-agent`; commit after every phase/iteration (user, 2026-10-19).
Bench context = `inseer-frontend/.ambicode/context`, backup `.local-docs/context` (never touch; `cmp` index.md after every run).
`node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs` 73 pass, search tests 22 pass, typecheck clean (2026-10-20). `npm run verify` not run since the navigator work.

## Navigator: where we are (2026-10-20)

User decisions: the navigator stays on **haiku** (frequent scope subagent for all skills; a senior model refines; ±0.1 F1 vs sonnet is fine),
packaged as one tool, **no Bash** (too risky). Context exists only to make the navigator faster/cheaper; dropping it is a later decision.
Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plan: "navigator eval" (3146e432), next phase p12 (cleanup). Child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397) completed 2026-10-20.

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

```
variant                              6141   3571   6404   mean   R mean
bare (sonnet, no context)            .339   .521   .815   .558
sonnet V2.1 (4c6c84ad)               .33    .58    .86    .59
haiku 634cccd3 (cap 3 notes)         .144   .616   .744   .501   .443
haiku + map --folders/--near c46d76ae .050  .374   .738          .427
haiku 634 + map union 3d15eb34       .077   .355   .745          .356
haiku no context 4fef362f            .140   .465   .835   .480   .428
haiku cap 12 notes d5349924          .112   .536   .817   .488   .392
haiku evidence rule, cap 6 4fc7b3f   .140   .537   .815   .497   .447
haiku deepest notes 932b65e4         .185   .625   .815   .542   .503   <- current file
```

10 cases: bare R .530 P .543 F1 .505 $0.144; sonnet V2 F1 .518; sonnet V2.1 F1 .542 $0.128; context-only sonnet (pre-V2) F1 .396.
**haiku 932b65e4, 10x3 (2026-10-20, stamps 17-55-29..18-12-57): R .593 P .610 F1 .572 $0.054/run** ($1.61 total, 0 zero-score).

```
case   438  6141 5948 6292 5967 5164 6404 3571 6406 6086
haiku .470 .194 .517 .473 .766 .857 .852 .555 .610 .431
bare  .738 .339 .502 .159 .503 .589 .815 .521 .480 .400
V2.1  .500 .331 .499 .309 .514 .803 .833 .520 .500 .615
```
Weak: 6141 (R .185), 438 (R .833 but P .329, per-run .55/.62/.25), 6086 (vs V2.1 -.18). Haiku peak context ~25k, 7.6 tool calls/run.

### Findings

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.
- Haiku obeys numeric caps and step order (6/6), not floors ("use all N": 3/6) or print steps (0/21). It emits no text/thinking.
- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.
- ~80% of haiku's lost truth folders never appear in a read note; sonnet reaches them by iterating source Greps (~10 on 6141).
- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.
- Bench cost: ~$0.55 per variant (3 cases x3); the sonnet relay main session dominates.

- Evidence-rule variant (129c0ce + cap 6 in 4fc7b3f; current file): "a note line or a Grep hit is evidence", Glob only
  self-composed paths, keep users/used-by, same-kind siblings rule, drop only clearly unrelated, recall framing.
  Funnel moved toward sonnet: named/listed .72 (was .47-.60, sonnet .77); named without source hit .36 (was .09, sonnet .94);
  non-truth kept .21; Glob 0 in 12 runs. F1 flat (mean .497 vs .501): what haiku keeps is now mostly fine, but on 6141 it
  reads the wrong notes (exact module P .06 R .04). Sibling rule followed in 1 of 2 runs that read the sibling note.
  Bench cost ~$0.80 (includes one cap-3 set on 6141: F1 .187).

## Next step

1. Done: deepest-note variant (932b65e4; Stage A/B open the deepest matching index line, parents only when no child matches,
   matching `## Submodules` child first). 6141 truth-bearing opens 14/18 (was 2/18), 14-16 truth folders listed per run;
   naming is the remaining gap there (26/46 listed named). Bench R .503 meets the child plan target.
2. Done: 10x3 confirmation (child plan p4 complete): F1 .572 > V2.1 .542 > bare .505 at 1/3 of the cost.
3. Backlog (user, 2026-10-20): 6141 naming / source-search usage hop; 438 precision; 6086 vs V2.1.
4. Then: source-search iteration like sonnet (next Grep from the previous hits); decide on the context (user, later).
3. p12: dead code (learn/seed/`navigator` CLI), `npm run verify`, version bump.

## Eval setup (navigator)

- Cases `fe-vs-<id>-navigator`, generated by `evals/scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (gitignored); never run `evals:generate`
  without `NAV_CASES`/`NAV_BENCH` (it wiped the cases once; regenerated, grader names match for all 10).
- Run: `npm run evals -- --tag navigator --case fe-vs-<id>-navigator --runs N --max-cost-usd X`, one case per command, build first.
- Plugin arm: sonnet relay main session (`allowed_tools: [Agent]`) calls `ambicode:navigator` once. `run.mjs` strips

- Scoring: truth/answer collapsed to folders, ancestorShare 0.3; metrics in `results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`.
- Eval dir must stay under 20,000 entries (18,433 at last count; ~16-30 per case run).
- Bench leakage: inseer-frontend HEAD is after every truth commit (favours source search for all arms).

## Open

- Path-prefix tolerance in the scorer (bare answers without `main/` score 0) — not decided.
- Done 2026-10-20 (71449eda, 72c446bd): test-only exports removed, 153 unused exports unexported, guard in

**Что изменилось**
- `config validate --json` теперь возвращает `scout: {model, effort}`.
- `scaffold.mjs` выводит эту настройку в своём JSON.
- Шаг 2 `SKILL.md` передаёт эти значения в вызов Agent, вместо того чтобы модель сама читала YAML.

**Порядок, по которому выбирается модель сабагента.** Документации на это нет, порядок восстановлен по строкам бинарника `claude`:
```
Agent model param  >  frontmatter  >  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL  >  inherit
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE overrides all (run.mjs strips it in evals)
```

- при невалидном конфиге поле `scout` отсутствует.

- Передаёт ли модель в реальном прогоне оба параметра в вызов Agent. В старых трейсах был виден `model`, а `effort` нет. Это покажет первый прогон.
- В конфиге поле `model` принимает любую строку, а Agent примет только sonnet/opus/haiku/fable. Опечатка в конфиге всплывёт только в момент вызова. Можно ограничить схему этим перечнем — это мелкая правка, сделаю, если скажете.

python3 - <<'E'
p='evals/README.md'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("| init-auto-ts |")
b=s.index("The init cases share their graders")
rows='''| init-auto-ts | ts-service-lendbox (32 modules) | TypeScript service by bounded context with a shared kernel, jest and eslint declared not installed; drafts for importing a context only through `index.ts`, `<context>.<past-tense-verb>` event names, deps-first use-case factories, `createX` returning `Result` |
| init-auto-python | py-service-tidewatch (30 modules) | layered domain/app/infra/api with a `plugins/sources/` directory of 12 sibling adapters; drafts for `TW-nnn` error codes, `test_<module>__<behaviour>` names, keyword-only arguments, `PLUGIN = SourcePlugin(...)` per adapter |
| init-auto-go | go-module-parcelhub (31 modules) | flat `cmd/` plus `internal/` with many small packages and one chain nested five levels; drafts for `pkg.Func: %w` wrapping, an injected Clock, constructors over `internal/core` interfaces, `var _ core.X = (*T)(nil)` assertions |
| init-auto-jvm | jvm-gradle-seedvault (34 modules) | hexagonal Kotlin across seven Gradle subprojects (domain, application, four adapters, bootstrap); drafts for value-class ids, `Outcome.Rejected` instead of exceptions, structured log key-values, `operator fun invoke` use cases |
| init-auto-monorepo | monorepo-rust-ts-kiln (30 modules) | three projects (Rust workspace `engine/crates/*`, Express `dashboard/` with a generated client, Python `tools/`) and a vendored `vendor/`; drafts for `_dc` units, `expect("invariant: ...")`, `register(app)` route modules, `impl std::error::Error` per crate; the generated client must be excluded |

'''
s=s[:a]+rows+s[b:]
old=s[s.index("The init cases share their graders"):s.index("## Change or add a case")]
new='''The init cases share their graders (`evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs`); each case directory also holds `expected-config.yaml` and `truth.json`, the result init should reach, the planted conventions with quotes, the contributor document and `modules` (the module notes `context tree` prints for the fixture, computed by the same function). Written conventions sit in the fixture's CONTRIBUTING.md, inferred ones only in code. Each fixture is about 30 modules (a module is a directory with three or more source files below it) in its own architecture, so the scout is tested on a tree the size of a real one. `node evals/scripts/cases.mjs --case 'init-*'` rewrites just these cases and leaves the navigator cases alone. `init-cases.test.mjs` checks them at no cost; no paid run has scored them yet.

Scout-quality graders (deterministic, `scoutGraders` in `init-cases.mjs`):

- `modules-linked-<i>-of-<n>`: regex on `index.md` with one lookahead per module link, six modules per grader, so the score shows how much of the tree was written. `context write` refuses an index link to a missing note, so a link proves the note exists; one `file_exists` per module would be about 30 graders per case. `deepest-module-note` is a `file_exists` on the deepest note.
- `index-links-every-module` (weight 2): the same lookaheads for the whole tree. `index-has-no-extra-notes`: `count:N` on module links, N = the module count, which catches notes the tree does not have.
- `contributor-doc-read`: `tool_used` Read of `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The trace file lists a subagent's own calls (`parent_tool_use_id` set), but nothing in the harness documentation or schema says `tool_used` counts them, so a pass may come from the main session's read alone.
- `conventions-descriptive`: `conventions.md` has no `must`, `never` or `always`; the `context-conventions` grader holds that the file exists.
- `draft-<convention>`: one tight pattern per planted convention on the draft pack the run writes, which is where the scout's conventions end up (`--auto` returns them to the main session, not to disk). A pattern needs a token only the code or the document shows, and the test feeds each one a paraphrase of the rule (passes) and a guess made from folder names (fails).

'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E

input.message:
All five init fixtures are rebuilt to about 30 modules, each in its own architecture, with scout-quality graders on every case. Commit `72db5f9c` ("evals: ~30-module init fixtures with distinct architectures, scout graders") holds only my files plus the regenerated `evals/cases/init-auto-*` dirs. Tests and typecheck pass at $0; Go and Kotlin were never compiled (no toolchain).

**Fixtures** (all in `fixtures/init-stacks.mjs`; module counts from `context tree`, files include tests and docs):

| Case | Architecture | Modules | Files | Depth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ts (new fixture `ts-service-lendbox`) | Node service by bounded context (catalog, members, lending, billing, notifications) over a shared kernel and platform, imported only through each context's `index.ts` | 32 | 87 | 5 |
| python (`py-service-tidewatch`) | layered domain/app/infra/api, `plugins/sources/` with 12 sibling adapters | 30 | 95 | 5 |
| go (`go-module-parcelhub`) | flat `cmd/` + `internal/`, 25 small packages, chain `carrier/regional/sortline/belt/sensor` | 31 | 93 | 6 |
| jvm (`jvm-gradle-seedvault`) | hexagonal Kotlin over 7 Gradle subprojects, 7 roots | 34 | 93 | 10 (Kotlin package path) |
| monorepo (`monorepo-rust-ts-kiln`) | Rust workspace of 9 crates, Express dashboard, Python `tools/`, `vendor/`, `__generated__` client | 30 | 118 | 6 |

- **TS fixture:** `ts-feature-boundary` is still used by `src/` tests and `cases.mjs`, so I left it untouched and added the new one for `init-auto-ts` only. It is declared, not installed.
- **Conventions:** every case plants 2 written and 2 inferred, which is one more inferred than before, and the TS case follows the same 2+2. The written ones are in `CONTRIBUTING.md`:
  - ts: context imports only through `index.ts`; event names `<context>.<past-tense-verb>`
  - python: `TW-nnn` error codes; `test_<module>__<behaviour>` test names
  - go: `pkg.Func: %w` error wrapping; no `time.Now` outside `internal/clock`
  - jvm: value-class ids; `Outcome.Rejected` instead of exceptions
  - monorepo: `_dc` temperature names; `expect("invariant: ...")`
  - The inferred ones, which no document states:
    - ts: use-case factories `(deps) => async (input)`; `createX` returning `Result`
    - python: keyword-only args; `PLUGIN = SourcePlugin(...)` per adapter
    - go: `New` taking `core` interfaces; `var _ core.X = (*T)(nil)`
    - jvm: structured log key-values; `operator fun invoke` use cases
    - monorepo: `register(app)` route modules; `impl std::error::Error` per crate
- **Module size:** `context tree` folds any directory with fewer than 3 source files below it into its parent, so each leaf module is 3 small files, not 1-4. Total files stay under 150.

**Graders:** 39-49 deterministic per case, plus 1 llm in each:

| Case | Total | Deterministic | LLM |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts | 40 | 39 | 1 |
| python | 40 | 39 | 1 |
| go | 39 | 38 | 1 |
| jvm | 39 | 38 | 1 |
| monorepo | 49 | 48 | 1 |

New shared helper `scoutGraders` in `evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs`:
- **Module coverage:** I did not write one `file_exists` per module. I used `modules-linked-i-of-n` instead: a regex on `index.md` with one lookahead per module link, 6 modules per grader (5-6 graders per case). `context write` refuses an index link to a missing note, so a link proves the note exists. A single `file_exists` covers the deepest note.
- **Whole index:** `index-links-every-module` (weight 2) is the same lookaheads over the whole tree. `index-has-no-extra-notes` uses `count:N`, which also catches notes the tree does not have.
- **Contributor doc:** `contributor-doc-read` is `tool_used` Read with `CONTRIBUTING\.md`.
- **Conventions:** `conventions-descriptive` is `not_contains` on `must|never|always`; the existing `context-conventions` grader still checks the file exists.
- **Planted conventions:** one tight `draft-<id>` pattern each (4 per case). They run on the draft pack Write, because `--auto` returns the scout's conventions to the main session, not to disk, and `last_message` is only the summary. I dropped the loose alternatives, including the old `Outcome` pattern. The test checks each pattern against a paraphrase of its rule (passes) and a guess made from folder names (fails).
- **Monorepo:** it also has `generated-excluded`, and the expected config now has a third project, `tools`.
- **Expected modules:** `truth.json` gets `modules` (the expected note paths) and `contributorDocument`. `modulesOf()` computes them with `buildModuleTree`, and the test asserts they equal what the real `context tree` prints.
- **Weights:** `modules-linked-*` are 1 each, `index-links-every-module` is 2, the other new graders 1. The case version is bumped to 2.

**Subagent tool calls and `tool_used`:** I could not establish this. The trace jsonl lists the scout's own Read/Bash calls with `parent_tool_use_id` set (checked in `evals/cases/results/traces/plugin/2026-10-20T19-30-46-940Z`). Nothing I found in the harness schema or docs says `tool_used` counts them. So `contributor-doc-read` may pass on a main-session read alone. I kept it as `tool_used` Read as you asked and noted the uncertainty in `evals/README.md`. The scout recipe does not require reading `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so this grader may fail for a good scout.

**$0 checks:**
- All 5 fixtures materialize and take the scaffold, and the expected configs pass `config validate` and `config packs`.
- Python: 9 pytest pass and ruff is clean. Monorepo Rust: `cargo test` (3 pass), `cargo clippy` (no warnings) and `cargo fmt --check` are all clean, and the generated `engine/Cargo.lock` is embedded. Monorepo Python `tools`: 2 pytest pass, ruff clean. TS: `tsc --noEmit` is clean on the TS service `src`, and the monorepo dashboard files parse; the jest and vitest tests were not run (nothing is installed).
- The good run passes every deterministic grader. Empty, scaffold-only and one-fault runs fail the right ones: a dropped index link fails exactly one coverage group plus the whole-tree and count graders, and a `must` in `conventions.md` fails `conventions-descriptive`.
- Planted-quote verbatim test passes, including the new locations.
- `node evals/scripts/cases.mjs --case 'init-*'` wrote 5 cases. `evals/cases/navigator/` and `evals/bare/navigator/` are still 10 and 10.
- `node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs fixtures/*.test.mjs`: 95 pass, 0 fail. `npm run typecheck`: clean. I did not run the full `verify`.

**Open issues:**
- `init` cases are capped in `cases.mjs` at `max_turns: 24` and `timeout_seconds: 900` (not my file). The scout writes ~30 notes level by level, so that cap may be tight, but I didn't measure it.
- `modules-linked-*` assumes the scout's index covers every level within `maxIndexTokens` 5000. For the largest tree (jvm, 34) I did not measure whether the index fits; if not, the deeper groups fail for a budget reason, not a scout one.
- `evals/README.md` still says cases should have under 15 graders; the init cases already exceeded that before this change.

Все пять fixture выросли до ~30 модулей, у каждой своя архитектура, коммит `72db5f9c`. Проверки за $0 проходят: 95 тестов, 0 упали, typecheck чистый. Go и Kotlin не компилировались, потому что тулчейна нет.

| Кейс | Архитектура | Модулей | Файлов |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts (новая `ts-service-lendbox`) | Node-сервис по bounded contexts с общим ядром | 32 | 87 |
| python | слои domain/app/infra/api и 12 плагинов-адаптеров | 30 | 95 |
| go | плоский `internal/` и цепочка вложенности на 6 уровней | 31 | 93 |
| jvm | hexagonal, 7 Gradle-подпроектов | 34 | 93 |
| monorepo | 9 Rust crate, Express, Python `tools/`, `vendor/` и `__generated__` | 30 | 118 |

- **Конвенции.** В каждом кейсе заложено 4: две записаны в `CONTRIBUTING.md`, две видны только в коде. Старую `ts-feature-boundary` используют тесты в `src/`, поэтому её не трогали и для TS-кейса сделали новую fixture.
- **Грейдеры.** На кейс 38–48 детерминированных и 1 llm. Покрытие модулей проверяется по ссылкам в `index.md`: `context write` не даёт сослаться на заметку, которой нет. Отдельно проверяется, что в index нет лишних заметок.
- Плохие рабочие папки валят ровно те грейдеры, которые должны. Хорошая проходит все.

**Что нужно решить до прогона**
1. **Грейдеры конвенций проверяют не scout.** Они смотрят, записала ли основная сессия черновики rules. С `--auto` она их сейчас не пишет вообще, так что эти 4 грейдера будут падать при любом scout. Предлагаю добавить параллельно такие же точные шаблоны на `conventions.md`: его пишет сам scout. Черновые грейдеры оставить для p21. Это правка за $0.
2. **Не ясно, видит ли `tool_used` вызовы сабагента.** Если не видит, `contributor-doc-read` будет проверять основную сессию, а не scout. Это покажет первый прогон.
3. **Лимиты могут не подойти.** `max_turns` 24 и бюджет index в 5000 токенов не проверены на 30 модулях.
4. **Baseline p19 больше не годится:** он снят на старых маленьких fixture. Нужен новый sonnet baseline: 5 кейсов ×3. Моя оценка — $0.25–0.35 за прогон, всего около **$4–5**, лимит ставлю **$7**.

Делаю правку (1) и затем baseline ×3 с лимитом $7?

- Плохие рабочие папки валят ровно те грейдеры, которые должны. Хорошая проходит все.

144	/** The module notes the scout must write: exactly what `context tree` prints for the fixture, computed by the same function. */
145	export function modulesOf(truth) {
146	  const files = Object.keys(Object.assign({}, ...fixtureByName(truth.fixture).steps.map((step) => step.write ?? {})));
147	  const tree = buildModuleTree(files, { roots: rootsOf(truth), maxModules: maxModulesFor(CONTEXT_LIMITS) });
148	  return tree.modules.map((module) => ({ note: module.note, dir: module.path, depth: module.depth }));
149	}

152	export function expectedConfig(truth) {
153	  const run = { model: 'sonnet', effort: 'medium', timeoutMinutes: 15 };
154	  return stringify({

156	    id: truth.fixture,

165	    },

167	    projects: truth.projects.map((project) => ({
168	      id: project.id,
169	      root: project.root,
170	      paths: project.paths,
171	      ecosystem: { languages: project.languages, frameworks: project.frameworks, packageManager: project.packageManager },
172	      include: project.include,
173	      exclude: project.exclude,
174	      ignored: [],
175	      packs: project.packs,

177	      commands: {},

179	    })),

183	const truthJson = (truth) => `${JSON.stringify({

193	const CONFIG = '.ambicode/config.yaml';
194	const DRAFT_WRITE = String.raw`"file_path":"[^"]*\.ambicode/policies/drafts/[^"]*\.ya?ml"`;

196	const LIVE = String.raw`(^|\n)[^#\n]*`;

199	/** Modules per coverage grader: the score then says how much of the tree was written, not only whether all of it was. */
200	const MODULES_PER_GROUP = 6;
201	const CONTEXT = '.ambicode/context';
202	
203	/**
204	 * What the scout wrote, checked without a model. Coverage: `context write` refuses an index.md link to a missing note, so a link in
205	 * index.md proves the note exists; one lookahead grader per group of modules (a file_exists grader per module would be ~30 per case),
206	 * one for the whole tree, one count that catches notes the tree does not have, and a file_exists on the deepest note.
207	 * Facts: the contributor document was read, and conventions.md holds descriptions, no rule wording.
208	 */
209	export function scoutGraders(b, truth) {
210	  const { regex, tool, exists } = b;
211	  const modules = modulesOf(truth);
212	  const linked = (list) => `^${list.map((module) => `(?=[\\s\\S]*\\]\\(${escapeRegex(module.note)}\\))`).join('')}`;
213	  const groups = [];
214	  for (let i = 0; i < modules.length; i += MODULES_PER_GROUP) groups.push(modules.slice(i, i + MODULES_PER_GROUP));
215	  const deepest = modules.reduce((best, module) => (module.depth > best.depth ? module : best), modules[0]);
216	  return [
217	    ...groups.map((group, i) => regex(`modules-linked-${i + 1}-of-${groups.length}`, linked(group), { file: `${CONTEXT}/index.md` })),
218	    regex('index-links-every-module', linked(modules), { file: `${CONTEXT}/index.md`, weight: 2 }),
219	    regex('index-has-no-extra-notes', String.raw`\]\(modules/[^)\s]+\.md\)`, { file: `${CONTEXT}/index.md`, match: `count:${modules.length}` }),
220	    exists('deepest-module-note', `${CONTEXT}/${deepest.note}`),

222	    tool('contributor-doc-read', 'Read', 'CONTRIBUTING\\.md'),
223	    regex('conventions-descriptive', String.raw`\b([Mm]ust|[Nn]ever|[Aa]lways|MUST|NEVER|ALWAYS)\b`, { file: `${CONTEXT}/conventions.md`, match: 'not_contains' }),
