227	/** Deterministic graders first, one llm grader for the judgement no pattern carries. `b` is cases.mjs's builder set. */
228	export function initGraders(b, truth) {
229	  const { regex, tool, never, exists, llm } = b;
230	  const many = truth.projects.length > 1;
231	  const first = truth.projects[0];
232	  const graders = [
233	    tool('scaffold-ran', 'Bash', 'scaffold\\.mjs'),
234	    tool('scout-invoked', 'Agent', 'ambicode:scout'),
235	    tool('config-validated', 'Bash', 'config validate'),
236	    tool('config-packs-ran', 'Bash', 'config packs'),
237	    never('no-questions', 'AskUserQuestion', '.'),
238	    never('no-rules-route', 'Bash', 'route start rules'),
239	    exists('config-written', CONFIG),
240	    ...['overview', 'navigation', 'conventions', 'index'].map((name) => exists(`context-${name}`, `.ambicode/context/${name}.md`)),
241	    ...scoutGraders(b, truth),
242	    regex('gitignore-has-ambicode', String.raw`(^|\n)/?\.ambicode/?\s*(\n|$)`, { file: '.gitignore' }),
243	    regex('schema-version', `schemaVersion:\\s*${SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION}`, { file: CONFIG }),
244	    // Both forms: one project reads as a single `- id:` under projects, and a monorepo needs a second.
245	    regex(many ? 'projects-two-or-more' : 'projects-single', String.raw`\n\s*- id:[\s\S]*\n\s*- id:`, { file: CONFIG, match: many ? 'contains' : 'not_contains' }),
246	  ];
247	  for (const project of truth.projects) {
248	    const where = many ? `-${project.id}` : '';
249	    graders.push(
250	      regex(`ecosystem${where}`, `${LIVE}languages:[\\s\\S]{0,80}\\b${anyOf(project.languages.flatMap((l) => (l === 'kotlin' ? ['kotlin', 'java'] : [l])))}\\b`, { file: CONFIG }),
251	      regex(`root-or-paths${where}`, many ? `${LIVE}(root|paths):[\\s\\S]{0,40}${project.id}` : `${LIVE}paths:[\\s\\S]{0,40}${anyOf(project.paths.map((p) => p.replace(/\/$/, '')))}`, { file: CONFIG }),
252	      regex(`test-check${where}`, `${LIVE}(all|file):[^\\n]*(${project.checkPatterns.test})`, { file: CONFIG, weight: 2 }),
253	      regex(`lint-check${where}`, `${LIVE}(all|file):[^\\n]*(${project.checkPatterns.lint})`, { file: CONFIG }),
254	    );
255	    if (project.filePatterns.length > 0) {
256	      graders.push(regex(`file-placeholder${where}`, `${LIVE}file:[^\\n]*${anyOf(project.filePatterns)}[^\\n]*\\{file\\}`, { file: CONFIG }));
257	    }
258	  }
259	  // Rules are packs since config v5: init copies the built-ins it selects and writes no config rules.
260	  graders.push(
261	    exists('common-design-copied', packFile('builtin/common-design')),
262	    regex('policy-file-listed', 'policies/common/common-design\\.yaml', { file: CONFIG }),
263	    regex('no-misfit-pack', `builtin/${anyOf(truth.wrongPacks)}`, { file: CONFIG, match: 'not_contains' }),
264	    regex('no-config-rules', String.raw`source:\s*(scout|manual|web)|(^|\n)rules:|\n\s+instruction:`, { file: CONFIG, match: 'not_contains' }),
265	  );
266	  for (const pack of first.packs.filter((p) => !COMMON.includes(p) && truth.projects.length === 1)) graders.push(exists(`${pack.split('/')[1]}-copied`, packFile(pack)));
267	  if (truth.generated !== undefined) graders.push(regex('generated-excluded', String.raw`(exclude|ignored):[\s\S]{0,300}${truth.generated}`, { file: CONFIG }));
268	  if (truth.conventions.length > 0) {
269	    graders.push(tool('drafts-written', 'Write', DRAFT_WRITE));
270	    // --auto still drafts the scout's conventions (skills/init/SKILL.md step 5); it only skips the web search, the question and the rules route.
271	    for (const convention of truth.conventions) graders.push(tool(`draft-${convention.id}`, 'Write', `${DRAFT_WRITE}.*(${convention.draft})`));
272	  }
273	  const names = truth.projects.map((project) => project.id).join(', ');
274	  const wrong = truth.wrongPacks.map((p) => p.replace(/-$/, '')).join(', ');
275	  graders.push(llm('summary-and-pack-fit', `
276	PASS only if all hold:
277	- The final message names the project${many ? 's' : ''} found (expected: ${names}; ${truth.stack}) and the checks found for ${many ? 'each' : 'it'} (${truth.projects.map((p) => Object.keys(p.checkPatterns).join('/')).join(' and ')}), says which checks or commands are missing, and lists the context files written.
278	- It reports that config validate passed, or lists its errors; it does not claim success while showing errors.
279	- The policy packs it says were chosen fit the stack: the common-* packs are plausible anywhere${truth.projects.some((p) => p.packs.some((id) => !COMMON.includes(id))) ? `, and ${[...new Set(truth.projects.flatMap((p) => p.packs.filter((id) => !COMMON.includes(id))))].join(', ')} fit${truth.projects.length === 1 ? 's' : ''} the named project` : ''}. Any ${wrong} pack is a misfit.
280	FAIL otherwise.`));
281	  return graders;
282	}

284	export function initCases(b) {
285	  return INIT_TRUTHS.map((truth) => ({

288	    tags: ['init'],

291	    prompt: '/ambicode:init --auto',
292	    bare: null,

`/ambicode:init --auto` finished for `tidewatch`, and `config validate` returned ok.

- **Project:** `tidewatch` is a Python project using uv. It covers `src/tidewatch`, includes `src/**/*.py` and excludes `tests/**`.
- **Packs:** I added seven built-in packs: `common-checks`, `common-code`, `common-design`, `common-errors`, `common-security`, `common-verification` and `python-quality`. They are copied into `.ambicode/policies/`.
- **Checks found:**
  - `test`: `uv run pytest`
  - `lint`: `uv run ruff check src tests`
- **Checks missing:** there is no `dev` or other command, so `commands` is empty.
- **Context files:** the scout wrote `.ambicode/context/` with `overview.md`, `navigation.md`, `conventions.md`, `index.md` and 30 module notes under `modules/src/tidewatch/`. It reported no remaining problems.
- **Rule drafts:** none are waiting. `--auto` skips the rules route, so I didn't draft any.
- **Open questions:**
  - The scout didn't read `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which may state written rules.
  - It didn't inspect `tests/`, so `conventions.md` says only that tests live in `tests/`.
  - The module notes were written from file names alone, not from the code.
  - Two candidate conventions came from `README.md`: layers import inward only, and run pytest and ruff before finishing. I didn't turn them into rules.

The config file was reformatted on disk after I wrote it, with flow-list spacing and comment placement changed. The contents are the same.

**Result: the scout never read CONTRIBUTING.md in any of the 15 runs, and it wrote the planted conventions in 3 of 60 cases.** Whole eval spend is $3.94 of the $7 budget. Part A is committed. Part B ran as asked with nothing changed.

**A) Commit fab46d92** "evals: scout convention graders on conventions.md", Opus co-author line, 22 explicit paths only.
- `scoutGraders` in `evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs` now emits `scout-convention-<id>` beside the existing graders. It uses the same `draft` pattern with target `{file: .ambicode/context/conventions.md}`. `draft-<id>` is unchanged.
- `init-cases.test.mjs` now writes a good conventions.md that paraphrases each convention without must/never/always. A paraphrase passes and the names-only guess fails, each grader checked on its own.
- Regenerated only with `--case 'init-*'`. Navigator dirs are still 10 and 10.
- `node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs fixtures/*.test.mjs`: 95/95 pass. `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- `find evals | wc -l`: 1615 before the runs, 2793 after.

**B) Table** (3 runs per case; stamps `2026-10-20T…`)

| case | score r1/r2/r3 (mean) | $/run | scout $/run | scout turns / calls (tree, --level, --index, write, Read, other) | main turns | duration s | max_turns / timeout |

| monorepo | .759/.776/.810 (.782) | .271 | .192 | 8.3 / 9.3 (1, 2.0, 0, 3.3, 2.0, 1) | 7.7 | 89/87/88 | none |

- Tool-call figures are per-run means. `--level` counts the loop `for n in 1 2 3` as one call.
- Scout $ is about 75% of the run cost. It comes from my own script, `/tmp/an/an.mjs`, not `breakdown.mjs`. It uses first-seen usage per message id, with output tokens estimated as chars x 0.52. It uses breakdown.mjs's prices, so cache writes at $4/Mtok overstate the scout slightly.
- Sources: `evals/cases/results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json` and `traces/plugin/<stamp>/<case>-N.jsonl`.
- Stamps: ts 21-55-10-444Z, python 21-56-42-600Z, go 21-58-02-999Z, jvm 21-59-33-726Z, monorepo 22-01-24-533Z.
- Total cost by case: ts $0.840, python $0.663, go $0.736, jvm $0.884, monorepo $0.813.
- The per-case `max-cost-usd 1.4` cap was never close.

**Scout quality** (x/3 runs unless noted)
- Module coverage graders passed: ts 6/6, go 6/6 and jvm 6/6 in all 3 runs. python and monorepo pass 5/5 in all 3. `index-links-every-module` passes 15/15.
- `index-has-no-extra-notes`: passes in ts, python and go (3/3 each). It fails 3/3 in jvm and monorepo.
  - jvm indexes 41 notes against 34 expected, and monorepo 33 against 30.
  - The extras are per-root `modules/<root>/overview.md` notes, for example `modules/adapters/cli/overview.md`. That is probably a truth-set gap for multi-root cases. I did not verify why the scout needs them.
- scout-convention written: 0/6 in ts, python, go and jvm. monorepo is 3/6 (`deci-celsius-names` in runs 2 and 3, `invariant-expect` in run 3).
- scout-convention inferred: 0/6 in every case, monorepo included.
- `contributor-doc-read`: false 15/15.
- `conventions-descriptive`: passes 12/15. It fails in ts-1, ts-3 and go-3 because conventions.md was never written.
  - `context-conventions` also fails in those same 3 runs.
  - Each of those scouts wrote only overview, navigation and index.
- `context write` `check.problems`:
  - In 8 of 15 runs the first write reported 3 to 23 problems (ts 14, python 6 to 11, go 23, jvm 7, monorepo 3). Every one was `submodule-link`.
  - The retry then wrote with 0 problems.
  - I parsed the `?` runs only partly. Every final write that I could read had 0 problems.

**Did `tool_used` count the scout's own Read?**
- The scout never read CONTRIBUTING.md. Its Reads are `templates/context-format.md` and `README.md` only.
- The main session did not read it either (0 Reads in all 15 runs). The grader's "Read called 0x" is therefore consistent with the facts.
- Whether `tool_used` counts subagent calls stays unresolved. No run had a scout Read matching a grader pattern, so these runs cannot test it.
- In monorepo the scout's Bash commands contain the word CONTRIBUTING, but only inside heredoc text, not as a read.
- Main-session final messages admit it. For example python-1 says "The scout didn't read CONTRIBUTING.md".

**Index budget**
- `index.md` sizes by chars/4: 969 to 1811 tokens (ts about 1250, python about 1150, go about 980, jvm 1700 to 1810, monorepo about 1220). The limit is 5000.
- The budget was not hit in any run. No coverage failure comes from it.

**Agent call parameters**
- The scaffold JSON carried `"scout":{"model":"sonnet","effort":"medium"}` in the run I checked (ts-1).
- The Agent call passed `model: "sonnet"` in 15/15 runs. It passed `effort` in 0/15.
- The skill did not forward effort.

**Failed graders, grouped**
- **Scout gap:**
  - 57 of 60 `scout-convention-*` graders (of the 3 hits above)
  - the 3 missing conventions.md files
  - the scout never reading CONTRIBUTING.md
  - the scout writing module notes "from file names alone" (the main session's own words)
- **Main-session gap:**
  - `drafts-written` 15/15 and `draft-*` 60/60. The main session says `--auto` skips drafting.
  - `test-check`, `lint-check` and `file-placeholder` in ts-3.
  - `projects-single` in jvm 3/3, `root-or-paths` in jvm 2/3, and `lint-check-engine` in monorepo 2/3. All of these are config.yaml content written by the main session.
- **Grader or truth issue:**
  - `index-has-no-extra-notes`, 6 fails, likely from the per-root notes above.
  - The `draft-*` graders are structurally unreachable for `--auto`.
  - `summary-and-pack-fit` failed 12/15 with no explanation, only "judge votes: FAIL FAIL FAIL". The python-1 final message looks reasonable. I did not investigate this one.
- **Harness:** none. Errors were null in all 15 runs.

Not done: I did not diagnose the `summary-and-pack-fit` judge failures or the per-root extra notes. I did not rerun anything.

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted

- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.

Новый sonnet baseline готов: средняя оценка 0.733, $0.262 за прогон, scout забирает около 75% цены. Главный провал scout: он ни разу не прочитал `CONTRIBUTING.md` (0 из 15 прогонов) и почти не находит заложенные конвенции. Грейдеры `scout-convention-*` на `conventions.md` закоммичены (`fab46d92`), все 15 прогонов стоили $3.94 при лимите $7.

```
case      runs            mean  $/run  scout $/run  scout turns
ts        .745 .745 .617  .702  .280   .209         8.0
python    .745 .745 .745  .745  .221   .167         7.7
go        .783 .783 .696  .754  .245   .196         9.0
jvm       .696 .674 .674  .681  .295   .243         9.3
monorepo  .759 .776 .810  .782  .271   .192         8.3
```

**Scout**
- **Конвенции.** Из 30 записанных в документации scout нашёл 3, все в монорепо. Из 30 видимых только в коде не нашёл ни одной. В 3 прогонах из 15 он вообще не создал `conventions.md`.
- **Модули.** Покрытие полное в 15 из 15 прогонов. Index весит 1–1.8k токенов, до бюджета в 5000 далеко.
- **Лишние записи.** В 8 прогонах из 15 первая запись контекста получала замечания `submodule-link`, scout её переписывал.

**Ответы на открытые вопросы**
- **Ходы.** Лимита в 24 хода хватает: основная сессия делает 7–8 ходов, ни один прогон в лимиты не упёрся.
- **Видит ли `tool_used` вызовы scout** — вопрос остался открытым. `CONTRIBUTING.md` не читал ни scout, ни основная сессия, так что проверять было не на чем.
- **Мой пробел в p2:** `model` доходит до вызова Agent в 15 из 15 прогонов, а `effort` — в 0 из 15. Scaffold выдаёт оба значения, но модель передаёт только `model`.

**Похоже на ошибки в грейдерах или truth**
- `index-has-no-extra-notes` падает в jvm и монорепо во всех трёх прогонах. Scout создаёт отдельную заметку `overview.md` для каждого корня проекта, а в truth их нет. Скорее всего, truth неполная, но проверка нужна.
- Судья `summary-and-pack-fit` поставил FAIL в 12 прогонах из 15 без объяснения. На вид ответ основной сессии нормальный. Этот судья стабильно шумит с самого начала.

**Пробелы основной сессии** (для p20 и p21): ни в одном прогоне не создано черновиков rules (0 из 15), в jvm неверно выделены проекты и пути, в монорепо нет `cargo clippy`.

**Предлагаю дальше**
1. **Мелкие правки за $0:**
   - передавать в Agent `effort` вместе с `model`, это одна фраза в шаге 2;
   - разобраться с per-root `overview.md` и поправить truth, если scout прав;
   - либо заменить судью конкретными критериями, либо выключить его до разбора.
2. **p3: haiku без изменений**, те же 5 кейсов ×3. Ожидаю около $1.5–2.5, лимит ставлю **$4**.

Рычаги (чтение contributor-доков, CLI для дерева и index, однократная запись общих файлов) оставляю на p4. Там же сравню, как они работают на sonnet и на haiku.

result:
Новый sonnet baseline готов: средняя оценка 0.733, $0.262 за прогон, scout забирает около 75% цены. Главный провал scout: он ни разу не прочитал `CONTRIBUTING.md` (0 из 15 прогонов) и почти не находит заложенные конвенции. Грейдеры `scout-convention-*` на `conventions.md` закоммичены (`fab46d92`), все 15 прогонов стоили $3.94 при лимите $7.

```
case      runs            mean  $/run  scout $/run  scout turns
ts        .745 .745 .617  .702  .280   .209         8.0
python    .745 .745 .745  .745  .221   .167         7.7
go        .783 .783 .696  .754  .245   .196         9.0
jvm       .696 .674 .674  .681  .295   .243         9.3
monorepo  .759 .776 .810  .782  .271   .192         8.3
```

**Scout**
- **Конвенции.** Из 30 записанных в документации scout нашёл 3, все в монорепо. Из 30 видимых только в коде не нашёл ни одной. В 3 прогонах из 15 он вообще не создал `conventions.md`.
- **Модули.** Покрытие полное в 15 из 15 прогонов. Index весит 1–1.8k токенов, до бюджета в 5000 далеко.
- **Лишние записи.** В 8 прогонах из 15 первая запись контекста получала замечания `submodule-link`, scout её переписывал.

**Ответы на открытые вопросы**
- **Ходы.** Лимита в 24 хода хватает: основная сессия делает 7–8 ходов, ни один прогон в лимиты не упёрся.
- **Видит ли `tool_used` вызовы scout** — вопрос остался открытым. `CONTRIBUTING.md` не читал ни scout, ни основная сессия, так что проверять было не на чем.
- **Мой пробел в p2:** `model` доходит до вызова Agent в 15 из 15 прогонов, а `effort` — в 0 из 15. Scaffold выдаёт оба значения, но модель передаёт только `model`.

**Похоже на ошибки в грейдерах или truth**
- `index-has-no-extra-notes` падает в jvm и монорепо во всех трёх прогонах. Scout создаёт отдельную заметку `overview.md` для каждого корня проекта, а в truth их нет. Скорее всего, truth неполная, но проверка нужна.
- Судья `summary-and-pack-fit` поставил FAIL в 12 прогонах из 15 без объяснения. На вид ответ основной сессии нормальный. Этот судья стабильно шумит с самого начала.

**Пробелы основной сессии** (для p20 и p21): ни в одном прогоне не создано черновиков rules (0 из 15), в jvm неверно выделены проекты и пути, в монорепо нет `cargo clippy`.

**Предлагаю дальше**
1. **Мелкие правки за $0:**
   - передавать в Agent `effort` вместе с `model`, это одна фраза в шаге 2;
   - разобраться с per-root `overview.md` и поправить truth, если scout прав;
   - либо заменить судью конкретными критериями, либо выключить его до разбора.
2. **p3: haiku без изменений**, те же 5 кейсов ×3. Ожидаю около $1.5–2.5, лимит ставлю **$4**.

Рычаги (чтение contributor-доков, CLI для дерева и index, однократная запись общих файлов) оставляю на p4. Там же сравню, как они работают на sonnet и на haiku.

13:1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
14:2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
15:3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
17:5. Level info, once per level before you write it: Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --level <n>` (the same roots as step 3; the roots' modules are level 1). It prints, for every folder of that level, a linked folder line and one line per unique file base name (the file name without the suffixes after its first dot) with the entity names its files declare; tests, stories, mocks, styles and templates are left out. Use it for each folder's purpose together with the heads you read.
18:6. Write level by level. After you have gathered one breadth-first level, write that level's notes, plus `overview.md` and `navigation.md` updated for everything seen so far (never `index.md` here), then go to the next level. Each write is one call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec and the same roots as step 3. The first write adds `--replace`; later writes omit it, so they add or update only the files in their bundle and keep the rest. `index.md` links may name only notes already written or in that bundle. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: fix those notes from what you just read and write that level again before going deeper. Never use Write.
22:`## Purpose` has 2 bullets of at most 25 words each: the first says what the folder is for in the product's own words (the titles and abbreviations read in step 4, the entity names from step 5), the second says what roles it contains (the kinds of things its subfolders and base names are); neither restates the folder name or says "source files of ... scope". Write `## Key files` and `## Folders` as empty headings: `context write` fills them from the code, and it generates the `Root:` field, so write paths relative to the module directory or none. To describe a file, repeat its generated bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares; to describe a folded folder, repeat its generated bullet as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>`. Each description is at most 12 words and comes from the names and level info only, with no extra file reads.
26:`index.md` is the folder tree the spec describes: its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, and where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Build it from the output of Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --index` (the same roots): it prints the whole `index.md` body within the `context.maxIndexTokens` budget: one line per module folder with the first Purpose bullet of its note and the names of its Key files, shallowest levels first, so every note it links must already be written. Copy it as printed and add nothing else. Run it only after the last level's notes are written, then write `index.md` alone in one more `context write` call (no `--replace`), so every description is read from a written note.

Judge only the final message, with these checks.
1. Packs: it names the policy packs chosen. PASS if every pack it names is a common-* pack${fits.length > 0 ? `, one of ${fits.join(', ')}, or another pack of the same family (express-*, python-*, angular-*) for the project of that stack` : ''}. FAIL if it names a pack for another stack: ${wrong}.

PASS only if both hold. Do not fail it for omitting a fact; other graders check names, checks, context files and drafts.`));
"""

open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

**A: $0 fixes (commit 9e16d796)**
1. `skills/init/SKILL.md` step 2 now reads: "with Agent `model` and `effort` from scaffold `scout` (user-set)". The body is 1531 bytes against the 1536 cap. Cause: the Agent tool's own schema says to set `effort` only when a user or skill explicitly asks, so the old wording was read as optional. This fix did not work (see B).
2. `index-has-no-extra-notes`: per-root `overview.md` notes are intended. `noteOf()` in `src/modules/context/context.ts` gives every module with submodules `modules/<dir>/overview.md`. The truth was wrong. It computed the tree from the project `paths` (e.g. `adapters/cli/src/main/`), but the scout picks top-level directories from `git ls-files` (`agents/scout.md` step 2).
   - I added `scoutRoots` to the jvm truth (`adapters application bootstrap domain`) and the monorepo truth (`engine dashboard tools`); `rootsOf()` uses it when present.
   - Counts now: jvm 41 and monorepo 33, equal to the links in all 6 baseline indexes I counted. ts, python and go are unchanged at 32, 30 and 31.
   - I raised the test's module-count ceiling from 36 to 42 and commented why. The coverage-group graders were regenerated (jvm 7 groups, monorepo 6).
3. `summary-and-pack-fit` is split. Six regex graders on the last message, each weight 1: `summary-names-projects`, `-lists-checks`, `-says-missing`, `-lists-context`, `-says-drafts`, `-reports-validate`. The llm grader keeps two checks, weight 2 unchanged: (a) every pack named is common-*, a pack of the project's own family, or not from the misfit list, and (b) no claim that an unrun check passed or that validate passed while listing errors.
   - Why it failed 12/15: the old rubric demanded the truth's project id. The jvm summaries name `domain`/`adapters`, not `seedvault`. It also bundled everything into one unexplained vote. I read the ts, jvm and monorepo baseline messages; the facts the new graders check are all in them.
   - A test pattern for the jvm project name is `seedvault|domain|adapters` (`nameInSummary` on the truth).
4. Tests, all green: `node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs fixtures/*.test.mjs` (95 pass, 0 fail), the related `src/` tests (`skill-content`, `context-cost`, skills, `architecture`: 297 pass), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`.
   - I updated `init-cases.test.mjs` for last-message regex targets and the new roots.
   - The cases were regenerated with `node evals/scripts/cases.mjs --case 'init-*'`; navigator dirs are still 10/10.
   - Staged only the three code files plus the five `evals/cases/init-auto-*` dirs, no `.plugin-master/` or results. The three code files are `skills/init/SKILL.md`, `evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs` and `evals/scripts/init-cases.test.mjs`.

**B: haiku scout, stopped after case 1**
- **Mechanism:** I temporarily changed the `scout:` default in `templates/config.yaml` to `model: haiku`, then ran `npm run build`. The plugin under test is the repo itself, so `scaffold.mjs` copies that template. The template is now restored from `git show HEAD:templates/config.yaml`, rebuilt, and `git diff --stat templates/` is empty. `git status` shows only `.plugin-master/` changes. Nothing haiku-related was committed.
- **Eval dir:** `find evals | wc -l` was 2825 before and is 3018 after.
- **Command run:** `npm run evals -- --case init-auto-ts --runs 3 --max-cost-usd 0.8`, stamp 2026-10-20T22-13-41-555Z.
- **Proof of haiku:** all 3 Agent calls had `"model":"haiku"`. Scout assistant messages report `claude-haiku-5-5` (17, 16 and 12 messages), and main-session messages report `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
- **Stop reason:** `effort` was passed in 0/3 Agent calls, even with the new wording. The scout therefore inherits the session effort (eval default is low, not medium). Medium effort is not tested, and the haiku numbers are confounded.
- **Decision for you:** how to get `effort` into the call (a hard-coded value in the skill, or a harness change), then whether to run the other four cases. I did not spend more.

ts case, 3 runs, haiku scout (sonnet v2 mean was .733, $0.262/run, scout about $0.20):

| run | score | cost | duration | main turns | scout turns / tool calls | scout est. output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | .774 | $0.126 | 122s | 4 | 17 / 20 | 13.9k |
| 2 | .774 | $0.125 | 122s | 4 | 16 / 18 | 13.5k |
| 3 | .755 | $0.110 | 104s | 3 | 12 / 17 | 11.8k |

- **Totals:** mean .768, $0.120/run, $0.361 for the whole run. Scout cost per run was not computed.
- **Estimate method:** output tokens are chars x0.52, not measured. Turns are deduped by message id.
- **Sonnet ts baseline:** I did not recompute it, so there is no per-case sonnet comparison.

Scout quality on ts (all three runs identical):
- **Context files:** `index.md`, `overview.md`, `navigation.md` and `modules/` were written; `conventions.md` was missing in 3/3.
- **Conventions:** the scout never read `CONTRIBUTING.md` (`contributor-doc-read` 0 calls). So `context-conventions`, `conventions-descriptive` and the four `scout-convention-*` graders failed in every run.
- **Drafts:** no drafts were written (`drafts-written` and the four `draft-*` graders failed), because there were no scout conventions to draft from.
- **Module coverage:** the `modules-linked` and `index-links-every-module` graders did not fail in any run. That is only from the failed-grader list; I did not read the per-module scores.
- **Summary graders:** the new regex graders passed except `summary-reports-validate`, which failed in run 3. `summary-and-pack-fit` passed 3/3.
- **Not checked:** `check.problems`, the scout's final-report format, and a haiku-specific gap analysis. I did not read the scout's final report in these traces.
- **Failures by owner:** scout, 11 graders (conventions, 4 scout-convention, contributor-doc-read, conventions-descriptive, context-conventions, plus the drafts that depend on them). Main session, 0 clear cases. Grader, 1 (`summary-reports-validate` in run 3, possibly a wording miss).
- **Sonnet comparison:** the sonnet baseline ts message said "the scout reported no conventions" and also did not read `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so this gap is not haiku-specific.
- **Cost/speed:** about half the sonnet cost per run ($0.12 vs $0.262) at a similar score, with the missing conventions as the quality gap.

Biggest haiku-specific gaps so far, from 1 case only:
1. `effort` is dropped by the main session (0/3 here, 0/15 in the baseline).
2. The scout skips `conventions.md` and the contributor doc entirely.
3. Not yet established; no other cases were run.

## Current version

0.6.1 (bumped in 33c2a5b4 after p12 cleanup; `npm run verify` green 2026-10-20, 1236 tests 0 fail). Branch `navigator-agent`; commit after every phase/iteration (user, 2026-10-19).
Bench context = `inseer-frontend/.ambicode/context`, backup `.local-docs/context` (never touch; `cmp` index.md after every run).
`node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs` 73 pass, search tests 22 pass, typecheck clean (2026-10-20). `npm run verify` not run since the navigator work.

## Navigator: where we are (2026-10-20)

User decisions: the navigator stays on **haiku** (frequent scope subagent for all skills; a senior model refines; ±0.1 F1 vs sonnet is fine),
packaged as one tool, **no Bash** (too risky). Context exists only to make the navigator faster/cheaper; dropping it is a later decision.
Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plan: "navigator eval" (3146e432), next phase p12 (cleanup). Child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397) completed 2026-10-20.

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

```
variant                              6141   3571   6404   mean   R mean
bare (sonnet, no context)            .339   .521   .815   .558
sonnet V2.1 (4c6c84ad)               .33    .58    .86    .59
haiku 634cccd3 (cap 3 notes)         .144   .616   .744   .501   .443
haiku + map --folders/--near c46d76ae .050  .374   .738          .427
haiku 634 + map union 3d15eb34       .077   .355   .745          .356
haiku no context 4fef362f            .140   .465   .835   .480   .428
haiku cap 12 notes d5349924          .112   .536   .817   .488   .392
haiku evidence rule, cap 6 4fc7b3f   .140   .537   .815   .497   .447
haiku deepest notes 932b65e4         .185   .625   .815   .542   .503   <- current file
```

10 cases: bare R .530 P .543 F1 .505 $0.144; sonnet V2 F1 .518; sonnet V2.1 F1 .542 $0.128; context-only sonnet (pre-V2) F1 .396.
**haiku 932b65e4, 10x3 (2026-10-20, stamps 17-55-29..18-12-57): R .593 P .610 F1 .572 $0.054/run** ($1.61 total, 0 zero-score).

```
case   438  6141 5948 6292 5967 5164 6404 3571 6406 6086
haiku .470 .194 .517 .473 .766 .857 .852 .555 .610 .431
bare  .738 .339 .502 .159 .503 .589 .815 .521 .480 .400
V2.1  .500 .331 .499 .309 .514 .803 .833 .520 .500 .615
```
Weak: 6141 (R .185), 438 (R .833 but P .329, per-run .55/.62/.25), 6086 (vs V2.1 -.18). Haiku peak context ~25k, 7.6 tool calls/run.

### Findings

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.
- Haiku obeys numeric caps and step order (6/6), not floors ("use all N": 3/6) or print steps (0/21). It emits no text/thinking.
- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.
- ~80% of haiku's lost truth folders never appear in a read note; sonnet reaches them by iterating source Greps (~10 on 6141).
- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.
- Bench cost: ~$0.55 per variant (3 cases x3); the sonnet relay main session dominates.

- Evidence-rule variant (129c0ce + cap 6 in 4fc7b3f; current file): "a note line or a Grep hit is evidence", Glob only
  self-composed paths, keep users/used-by, same-kind siblings rule, drop only clearly unrelated, recall framing.
  Funnel moved toward sonnet: named/listed .72 (was .47-.60, sonnet .77); named without source hit .36 (was .09, sonnet .94);
  non-truth kept .21; Glob 0 in 12 runs. F1 flat (mean .497 vs .501): what haiku keeps is now mostly fine, but on 6141 it
  reads the wrong notes (exact module P .06 R .04). Sibling rule followed in 1 of 2 runs that read the sibling note.
  Bench cost ~$0.80 (includes one cap-3 set on 6141: F1 .187).

## Next step

1. Done: deepest-note variant (932b65e4; Stage A/B open the deepest matching index line, parents only when no child matches,
   matching `## Submodules` child first). 6141 truth-bearing opens 14/18 (was 2/18), 14-16 truth folders listed per run;
   naming is the remaining gap there (26/46 listed named). Bench R .503 meets the child plan target.
2. Done: 10x3 confirmation (child plan p4 complete): F1 .572 > V2.1 .542 > bare .505 at 1/3 of the cost.
3. Backlog (user, 2026-10-20): 6141 naming / source-search usage hop; 438 precision; 6086 vs V2.1.
4. Then: source-search iteration like sonnet (next Grep from the previous hits); decide on the context (user, later).
3. p12: dead code (learn/seed/`navigator` CLI), `npm run verify`, version bump.

## Eval setup (navigator)

- Cases `fe-vs-<id>-navigator`, generated by `evals/scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (gitignored); never run `evals:generate`
  without `NAV_CASES`/`NAV_BENCH` (it wiped the cases once; regenerated, grader names match for all 10).
- Run: `npm run evals -- --tag navigator --case fe-vs-<id>-navigator --runs N --max-cost-usd X`, one case per command, build first.
- Plugin arm: sonnet relay main session (`allowed_tools: [Agent]`) calls `ambicode:navigator` once. `run.mjs` strips
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL*` from the child env (the user's shell forces sonnet otherwise). Scaffold copies context + config.yaml.
- Scoring: truth/answer collapsed to folders, ancestorShare 0.3; metrics in `results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`.
- Eval dir must stay under 20,000 entries (18,433 at last count; ~16-30 per case run).
- Bench leakage: inseer-frontend HEAD is after every truth commit (favours source search for all arms).

## Open

- Path-prefix tolerance in the scorer (bare answers without `main/` score 0) — not decided.
- Done 2026-10-20 (71449eda, 72c446bd): test-only exports removed, 153 unused exports unexported, guard in
  `src/architecture.test.ts` ("exports only what another file imports", empty allowlist). Still open: todo test
  review-route.test.ts:343 (`--answer narrow` repeat-limit bug, task-lifecycle P3); unused exports in evals/scripts/*.mjs (low).

## Init + scout (plan d4d08796, started 2026-10-20)

p17 walkthrough done (read-only, $0; code steps run by hand on fixture ts-feature-boundary: all exit 0).
- Init = skill + scripts (no route); only the rules hand-off goes through the engine. Scout `agents/scout.md`: sonnet fixed
  in frontmatter, tools Bash/Read/Grep/Glob, writes `.ambicode/context/*` level by level via `context write`.
- `skills.init.scout` (model/effort) is read by no code; the model copies it into the Agent call (prose only).
- `config packs` rewrites `ignored` from disk (hand-written value lost, prints "ignored: none").
- Real inseer-frontend traces (9 sessions 10-12..10-19): scout 8-56 turns / 100-531s on the same repo (Bash dominates);
  main ~10 turns, ~370 of 467s are human waits. Token/cost figures in those traces unreliable; no $ baseline yet.
- Existing case `init-auto` in `evals/scripts/cases.mjs` (fixture ts-feature-boundary, 16 graders, never run). Needs 4 new
  fixtures on other stacks, per-case graders, a rule-draft grader. Unverified: its `allowed_tools` lacks Agent (scout grader).

p18 done (23adeb26): 5 cases `init-auto-{ts,python,go,jvm,monorepo}` from `evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs`, fixtures in
`fixtures/init-stacks.mjs`; generate with `node evals/scripts/cases.mjs --case 'init-*'` (navigator cases untouched, 10/10).
23-31 deterministic graders + 1 llm per case; `expected-config.yaml` + `truth.json` per case; 2-3 planted conventions
(written + inferred) per case except TS (none). $0 checks: good workspace passes, empty/bad fails (13 tests).
`Agent` added to init allowed_tools (harness withholds ungranted tools); same gap in review/plan/task/investigate limits, unchanged.
Not verified: Go/Kotlin not compiled, 24 turns/900s limits and llm rubrics untested on a model.

p19 smoke x1 (sonnet, 2026-10-20 stamps 19-27-27..19-31-45): ts .923 / python .871 / go .759 / jvm .862 / monorepo .857,

Правки закоммичены (`9e16d796`). Haiku-scout прогнали пока только на ts, затем агент остановился: модель так и не передала `effort` в вызов Agent, 0 из 3, даже после явной формулировки в шаге 2.

```
ts            score  $/run  scout turns  duration
sonnet v2     .702   .280   8            70-88s
haiku scout   .768   .120   12-17        104-122s
```

**Что видно по ts**
- Scout действительно работал на haiku (`claude-haiku-5-5`). Шаблон вернули к HEAD, `git diff` чистый.
- Прогон стоит вдвое меньше, но scout делает в 1.5–2 раза больше ходов, и прогон длится дольше.
- Haiku-scout, как и sonnet, не читает `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Файл `conventions.md` он не создал ни в одном из трёх прогонов. Этот пробел общий для обеих моделей, к haiku он не относится.
- **Оценки 0.768 и 0.702 сравнивать нельзя.** Между прогонами набор грейдеров изменился: судью разбили на regex-грейдеры, truth для per-root заметок исправили. Сравнимы метрики, которые не менялись: грейдеры scout (покрытие модулей, конвенции, `conventions.md`), цена и ходы.

**Что исправлено в `9e16d796`**
- Отдельные заметки `overview.md` для каждого корня задуманы форматом. Неправильной была truth, теперь она совпадает со всеми 6 index из baseline.
- Судья падал в основном потому, что требовал id проекта из truth, а jvm называет проекты иначе. Теперь 6 конкретных regex-грейдеров и короткий llm-грейдер на подбор packs.

**Что решить по `effort`.** Вызов Agent получает только `model`. В описании инструмента сказано ставить `effort` только по явной просьбе, и модель всё равно его опускает. Поэтому scout наследует effort сессии; в eval это low. Варианты:
1. **Бесплатно проверить, поддерживает ли frontmatter агента поле `effort:`** (рекомендую). Если поддерживает, задать effort там. Тогда он будет срабатывать надёжно, но перестанет настраиваться через config. Если не поддерживает, переходить к варианту 2.
2. Убрать `effort` из настройки `skills.init.scout`, и scout честно наследует effort сессии. Сейчас конфиг обещает управление, которого на деле нет.
3. Оставить как есть и мерить haiku на low. На ts уже видно, что и на low он работает.

Пока решаем с `effort`, haiku на остальные 4 кейса не запускаю. После решения прогон всех 4 кейсов ×3 стоит около **$1.5**, лимит ставлю $3.

Начать с проверки frontmatter?

  1. `effort` is dropped by the main session (0/3 here, 0/15 in the baseline).
  2. The scout skips `conventions.md` and the contributor doc entirely.

- Прогон стоит вдвое меньше, но scout делает в 1.5–2 раза больше ходов, и прогон длится дольше.
- Haiku-scout, как и sonnet, не читает `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Файл `conventions.md` он не создал ни в одном из трёх прогонов. Этот пробел общий для обеих моделей, к haiku он не относится.
- **Оценки 0.768 и 0.702 сравнивать нельзя.** Между прогонами набор грейдеров изменился: судью разбили на regex-грейдеры, truth для per-root заметок исправили. Сравнимы метрики, которые не менялись: грейдеры scout (покрытие модулей, конвенции, `conventions.md`), цена и ходы.

**Что исправлено в `9e16d796`**
- Отдельные заметки `overview.md` для каждого корня задуманы форматом. Неправильной была truth, теперь она совпадает со всеми 6 index из baseline.

3. Оставить как есть и мерить haiku на low. На ts уже видно, что и на low он работает.

---
name: scout
description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---
You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Follow this recipe exactly.

Walk the tree breadth-first: all folders of one level before any deeper. Visit each directory at most once in the whole run: keep a running list of visited directories and move on to one not on it. Locate names and files with Grep and Glob first; read content only when search results do not settle a module's purpose.

Never read a file whole (except the format spec in step 1): only heads or ranges with a line limit. Never read styles, tests or specs, mocks or fixtures, stories, nor generated, vendored, lock or build files.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only as heads with limit <= 40, only non-excluded ones, and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names and search. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language string catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms.
5. Level info, once per level before you write it: Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --level <n>` (the same roots as step 3; the roots' modules are level 1). It prints, for every folder of that level, a linked folder line and one line per unique file base name (the file name without the suffixes after its first dot) with the entity names its files declare; tests, stories, mocks, styles and templates are left out. Use it for each folder's purpose together with the heads you read.
6. Write level by level. After you have gathered one breadth-first level, write that level's notes, plus `overview.md` and `navigation.md` updated for everything seen so far (never `index.md` here), then go to the next level. Each write is one call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec and the same roots as step 3. The first write adds `--replace`; later writes omit it, so they add or update only the files in their bundle and keep the rest. `index.md` links may name only notes already written or in that bundle. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: fix those notes from what you just read and write that level again before going deeper. Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

`## Purpose` has 2 bullets of at most 25 words each: the first says what the folder is for in the product's own words (the titles and abbreviations read in step 4, the entity names from step 5), the second says what roles it contains (the kinds of things its subfolders and base names are); neither restates the folder name or says "source files of ... scope". Write `## Key files` and `## Folders` as empty headings: `context write` fills them from the code, and it generates the `Root:` field, so write paths relative to the module directory or none. To describe a file, repeat its generated bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares; to describe a folded folder, repeat its generated bullet as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>`. Each description is at most 12 words and comes from the names and level info only, with no extra file reads.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>` (the full note path is accepted: `context write` makes it relative), so a reader can find it from the parent. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

`index.md` is the folder tree the spec describes: its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, and where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Build it from the output of Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --index` (the same roots): it prints the whole `index.md` body within the `context.maxIndexTokens` budget: one line per module folder with the first Purpose bullet of its note and the names of its Key files, shallowest levels first, so every note it links must already be written. Copy it as printed and add nothing else. Run it only after the last level's notes are written, then write `index.md` alone in one more `context write` call (no `--replace`), so every description is read from a written note.

Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is for the commands in steps 2, 3 and 5 (`git ls-files`, `context tree` with and without `--level` or `--index`), the `context write` in step 6, and plain read-only listing (`ls`, `git ls-files`). Use Glob for file lookup.

- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).

A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).

Repo: /Users/KillBill/Documents/projects/mine/ai/ambicode (AMBICODE plugin). Follow its CLAUDE.md strictly: change existing code before adding, the whole job, tests with the change, typecheck per edit, `npm run verify` (foreground, timeout 600000) before commit. Never run git state commands (stash, checkout, reset, restore, switch, clean, revert); to restore a file write it from `git show HEAD:<path>`. Tuning must be generic: no ecosystem-, language- or fixture-specific terms in code, prompts or examples (an example resembling an eval case is a leak). The user approved the code change and a paid run, budget $5.

Context. The `ambicode:scout` agent (`agents/scout.md`, plus the `context` CLI in `src/cli` and `src/modules/context/`) maps a repo into `.ambicode/context/` (overview, navigation, conventions, index, modules/**). Evals: five init cases `init-auto-{ts,python,go,jvm,monorepo}` (~30 modules each, 2 written conventions in a contributor doc + 2 code-only conventions each; generator `evals/scripts/init-cases.mjs`). Measured (15 runs per arm):
- haiku scout: conventions.md written 0/15, planted conventions 0/60, ~15 turns, 6.3 `context write` calls/run (one per tree level), 1.5 failed writes/run (`check.problems`, mostly submodule-link), 110-162s per run, scout $0.017-0.027.
- sonnet scout: conventions.md 12/15, planted 3/60, ~8.5 turns, 3.3 writes/run, $0.14-0.20.
- contributor doc read: 0/30 in both arms. Prior research: overview/navigation/conventions re-emitted on every level write; `--index` output is copied verbatim into a write by the model; `--level N` fetched per level; `templates/context-format.md` (7.7 KB) read whole each run; haiku obeys numeric caps and step order and fixes reported problems, but skips optional "read/print" steps.

Implement both levers, changing existing code paths:
1. Conventions via the CLI, not prose: (a) `context write` reports a problem in its existing `check.problems` when the final context has no conventions.md (decide where "final" is detectable — e.g. when index.md is written or the set is complete; reuse the existing check mechanism); (b) `context tree` output lists the repo's top-level human-written guidance docs it finds (contributor/readme/architecture-style docs found by a generic rule, e.g. root-level and docs/ markdown files, capped) as plain facts, and the scout prompt step that gathers conventions says to read them. Keep conventions.md descriptive (no must/never/always) as today.
2. Fewer turns: (a) `context tree` returns all levels in one call (extend the existing command; drop the per-level fetch from the prompt); (b) `context write` builds index.md itself from the notes written (so the model no longer copies `--index` output) — keep `--index` only if something else needs it, otherwise remove it and its prompt step; (c) the prompt writes overview/navigation/conventions once, and module notes in as few writes as the size check allows (batch by size, not by level). Shorten `agents/scout.md` and `templates/context-format.md` where these changes make text obsolete; remove dead instructions (Grep/Glob-first steps never used). Keep the scout's final report format.
Tests for every behaviour change (CLI unit tests beside the existing context tests). Grep tests that assert on touched files. Then `npm run verify`. Commit explicit paths only (never `.plugin-master/`, never `evals/cases/results/`), message "scout: all-level tree, CLI-built index, conventions check, guidance docs", ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not bump the version.

Then run (after `npm run build`; `find evals | wc -l` first, stop if over 18,000; regenerate cases only if missing via `node evals/scripts/cases.mjs --case 'init-*'`, never `npm run evals:generate`), one command per case, foreground, timeout 600000, no loops/redirection:
- sonnet scout (default config): `npm run evals -- --case <case> --runs 2 --max-cost-usd 0.7` for all five cases;
- haiku scout: temporarily set the `scout:` default in `templates/config.yaml` to `model: haiku`, `npm run build`, run `npm run evals -- --case <case> --runs 2 --max-cost-usd 0.35` for all five, then restore the file from `git show HEAD:templates/config.yaml`, `npm run build`, confirm `git diff --stat templates/` is empty. Verify in the first haiku case that scout messages report a haiku model id.
If the first sonnet case shows the change broke the scout (no context, errors), stop and report before spending more.

Analyse both arms (scout messages are in the main jsonl with `parent_tool_use_id`; dedupe by message id; haiku cost exact from modelUsage, sonnet scout estimated chars x0.52 — say so). Previous numbers for comparison are in this brief; the grader set is unchanged since commit 9e16d796 so totals compare with the haiku p3 stamps (2026-10-20T22-13-41 ts, 22-20-30 py, 22-22-34 go, 22-24-48 jvm, 22-27-43 mono).

---
name: scout
description: Internal to /ambicode:init. Never invoke on your own initiative.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: sonnet
---
You map a repository cheaply and write learning context for future agents. Follow this recipe exactly.

Walk the tree breadth-first: all folders of one level before any deeper. Visit each directory at most once in the whole run: keep a running list of visited directories and move on to one not on it. Locate names and files with Grep and Glob first; read content only when search results do not settle a module's purpose.

Never read a file whole (except the format spec in step 1): only heads or ranges with a line limit. Never read styles, tests or specs, mocks or fixtures, stories, nor generated, vendored, lock or build files.

1. Read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/context-format.md` once (whole file). It is the spec for every file you write.
2. Bash `git ls-files | cut -d/ -f1 | sort | uniq -c` once. Pick the source roots from it (working code dirs such as `src/`, `lib/`, `app/`, `pkg/`, `packages/`; no root when sources sit at the repository root).
3. Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...]` once. It walks the roots at full depth, skips tests and generated files, and prints one line per module: its note path, directory, depth, file count and submodules. Exactly one note per module it prints, at the note path it gives (a module with submodules gets `modules/<dir>/overview.md`, a leaf `modules/<dir>.md`), no others.
4. Read the README head (Read, limit 40). Read other files only as heads with limit <= 40, only non-excluded ones, and only when a module's purpose cannot be inferred from names and search. Then find where user-visible names live, from the step 2 listing and Glob only: the base-language string catalog, the route or navigation table, menu and title definitions, whichever the repository has. Read each head (limit 60) for UI titles, abbreviations and synonyms.
5. Level info, once per level before you write it: Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --level <n>` (the same roots as step 3; the roots' modules are level 1). It prints, for every folder of that level, a linked folder line and one line per unique file base name (the file name without the suffixes after its first dot) with the entity names its files declare; tests, stories, mocks, styles and templates are left out. Use it for each folder's purpose together with the heads you read.
6. Write level by level. After you have gathered one breadth-first level, write that level's notes, plus `overview.md` and `navigation.md` updated for everything seen so far (never `index.md` here), then go to the next level. Each write is one call: `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context write --task init --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] <<'EOF'` ... `EOF`, using the `=== <path>` bundle format from the spec and the same roots as step 3. The first write adds `--replace`; later writes omit it, so they add or update only the files in their bundle and keep the rest. `index.md` links may name only notes already written or in that bundle. The JSON `check.problems` is the only check, run by that call. If it is not empty nothing was written: fix those notes from what you just read and write that level again before going deeper. Never use Write.

`conventions.md` records how the code is, not what it must be: no "must", "never" or "always" bullets; those are candidate rules.

`## Purpose` has 2 bullets of at most 25 words each: the first says what the folder is for in the product's own words (the titles and abbreviations read in step 4, the entity names from step 5), the second says what roles it contains (the kinds of things its subfolders and base names are); neither restates the folder name or says "source files of ... scope". Write `## Key files` and `## Folders` as empty headings: `context write` fills them from the code, and it generates the `Root:` field, so write paths relative to the module directory or none. To describe a file, repeat its generated bullet as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` with a name that file declares; to describe a folded folder, repeat its generated bullet as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>`. Each description is at most 12 words and comes from the names and level info only, with no extra file reads.

A module whose line has `submodules:` gets a `## Submodules` section with one bullet per submodule, `- <its note path> - <what that folder holds>` (the full note path is accepted: `context write` makes it relative), so a reader can find it from the parent. Do not repeat a submodule's files in the parent.

`index.md` is the folder tree the spec describes: its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, and where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. Build it from the output of Bash `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" context tree --root <dir> [--root <dir>...] --index` (the same roots): it prints the whole `index.md` body within the `context.maxIndexTokens` budget: one line per module folder with the first Purpose bullet of its note and the names of its Key files, shallowest levels first, so every note it links must already be written. Copy it as printed and add nothing else. Run it only after the last level's notes are written, then write `index.md` alone in one more `context write` call (no `--replace`), so every description is read from a written note.

Stay within the limits in the spec; keep bullets sorted; no hedging. Bash is for the commands in steps 2, 3 and 5 (`git ls-files`, `context tree` with and without `--level` or `--index`), the `context write` in step 6, and plain read-only listing (`ls`, `git ls-files`). Use Glob for file lookup.

Final message (returned to the caller, not written to disk), compact:
- `projects`: per project `{id, paths, include, exclude}` suggestions (`paths` are working code roots, never `.` unless sources sit at the root; `include`/`exclude` globs).
- `conventions`: up to 10 candidate rules, each `{rule, quote, location, basis}`: `quote` is 20+ characters copied verbatim from `location` (`path:line`), `basis` is `written` when a project document states it or `inferred` when you saw it in code. A candidate is not repeated in `conventions.md`, which keeps only descriptive facts.
- `context files`: files written, plus any remaining `check.problems`.
- `unknowns`: anything unclear worth asking the user (optional).

content.content:
# Context format (`.ambicode/context/`)

Learning context for agents: small, deduplicated, fixed-shape files so an agent reads only the one it needs.
Limits come from `context.maxFileTokens`, `context.maxIndexTokens` (`index.md` only) and `context.maxTotalTokens` in `.ambicode/config.yaml` (defaults 2500, 5000 and 60000; tokens = chars / 4).

## Kinds (the only paths `context write` accepts)
- `overview.md`: purpose, stack, layout of the repository, one screen.
- `navigation.md`: how to find things.
- `conventions.md`: how code is written here, as facts. A convention that became a rule (`.ambicode/policies/`) is not repeated here.
- `modules/<directory>.md` or `modules/<directory>/overview.md`: exactly one per module, at the note path `ambicode context tree` prints. A leaf module is its directory path relative to the repository root with `.md` appended (`src/app/features/dashboard` -> `modules/src/app/features/dashboard.md`); a module with submodules keeps its note inside its folder (`src/app/features` -> `modules/src/app/features/overview.md`). Segments are letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; no `..`. A module is a directory, at any depth under a source root, that holds source files itself or branches into two such directories. `ambicode context tree` lists them with their note paths. No other files.
- `index.md`: the grep target for ticket words, one file, see below.

## Per-file structure
- H1 = the file's purpose, one line, unique across all files. Exactly one H1.
- H2 sections fixed per kind, in this order, each heading at most once per file. Keep an empty section's heading, omit its bullets.
  - `overview.md`: `## Purpose` (1-2 bullets), `## Projects` (`- <id> - <path> - <what it is>`), `## Stack` (`- <tool>: <role>`).
  - `navigation.md`: `## How to read` (one bullet: list, open one file, Grep the name, Read with offset/limit; never Read whole large files), `## Entry points` (`- <path> - <role>`), `## Where things live` (`- <thing>: <path or glob>`), `## Naming`, `## Grep patterns` (`- <what>: <pattern>`).
  - `conventions.md`: `## Code`, `## Errors`, `## Tests`, `## Imports`; one convention per bullet.
  - module notes: `Root: <module dir from the repo root>` directly under the H1 (generated by `context write`; never write it; every other path in the note is relative to it), `## Purpose` (2 bullets: what the folder is for, then what roles it contains), `## Key files` (filled by `context write` from the code: `- <path relative to Root> - <Name>, <Name>, ...` per source file of the module itself, files with the most exported declarations first, within the file limit; do not write it, only a bullet that repeats a generated path as `- <path> - <name>(args): <what it does>` is kept), `## Folders` (filled by `context write`; write only the empty heading: the folders below the module that hold source files but are not modules, one bullet each, `- <dir relative to Root>/ - <base name>, <base name>, ...`, so every source folder is named in some note; a bullet repeated as `- <dir>/ - <base name>, ...: <what the folder holds>` is kept), `## Submodules` (`- <child note path relative to this note's directory> - <what that folder holds>`, e.g. from `modules/a/b/overview.md` the child `modules/a/b/c.md` is `c.md` and `modules/a/b/c/overview.md` is `c/overview.md`; `context write` rewrites a full `modules/...` path to this form and reports `submodule-link` for one that names no note; only for a module that has child modules), `## Depends on`, `## Gotchas`.
- `index.md`: H1, then the folder tree of the modules, nothing else. One line per module folder, indented two spaces per tree level (roots are level 1), as a link to that folder's note: `- [<dir>](<note path>)`, where the link text is the folder path relative to the folder line above it (a root folder keeps its full path) and the link target is always the full note path; the full folder path is the target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`. Each line may end with ` - <description>`: the first `## Purpose` bullet of that folder's note, cut at 12 words, and then ` | <Name>, <Name>, ...`: the names of that note's `## Key files` bullets without their paths, deduplicated, the first 8 then `+N` (both generated from the notes on disk; a folder whose note is missing or lacks the section has no such part; names without a description give `- [<dir>](<note path>) | <names>`). A child folder's line follows its parent's line. There are no file lines: files and entities are in the notes' `## Key files` and `## Folders`. Every link must name a note of the bundle or already written. Folders are listed level by level, parents before children, shallowest first, up to the last whole level that fits the budget; deeper folders are reached through the parent note's `## Submodules` links. No other lines: no aliases, no categories, no invented names. It has its own budget, `context.maxIndexTokens` (default 5000, not `maxFileTokens`) and counts toward `maxTotalTokens`. Its purpose is to define the hierarchy and boundaries of the project's functionality (which folder holds which files and entities, where one folder ends and the next begins), so a later agent can map a ticket to the right scope. `ambicode context tree --level <n>` prints a level with its file lines for the scout; those lines are not index.md lines. Example:

  ```
  # Index
  - [src/billing](modules/src/billing/overview.md) - Invoices, tax and payment export | Invoice, InvoiceLine, totalOf, taxFor
    - [export](modules/src/billing/export.md) - CSV and PDF export of invoices | writeCsv, renderPdf
  - [src/auth](modules/src/auth.md) - Sign-in and session handling | Session, startSession
  ```
- Bullets sorted by path or name. Same repo state gives the same file.
- No hedging ("probably", "seems"), no dates, no drifting counts.
- No code bodies: code fences are refused; a signature is one line inside a bullet. Paths over prose.
- One fact in one file; point to another by relative path.

## Bundle format for `context write`
One call, bundle on stdin; each file starts with a line `=== <path relative to .ambicode/context/>`:

```
=== overview.md
# Overview of <repo>
## Purpose
- ...
=== modules/<note path from context tree>
# <directory> module
...
```

- `ambicode context write --replace` removes context files not in the bundle; without `--replace` only the named files change. `--root <dir>` (repeatable, the roots of `context tree`) tells it which module tree decides which module a file belongs to.
- Output is JSON `{written, removed, check: {problems}}`. Exit 1 and nothing written when `problems` is not empty (file too large, total too large, bad index.md line or indentation, index link to a missing note, duplicate H2 in a file, duplicate H1 across files, code fence, path outside the kinds). Fix with one more call naming only the changed files.
- `ambicode context list` prints path, H1 and approximate tokens per file, indented by folder; notes more than two levels down are counted on their level-1 parent.
- `ambicode context tree [--root <dir>...]` prints the modules of the source roots at full depth (note path, directory, depth, file count, submodules); it writes nothing.
- `ambicode context tree --root <dir> --index` prints the index.md body described above, built from the notes already written.
- `ambicode context tree --root <dir> --level <n>` prints one level of that tree in the index.md shape: each folder of the level (roots are level 1) as a linked line, then one line per unique file base name with the names its files declare. Companions (tests, stories, mocks, styles, templates) are left out. Names beyond 8 per base name are counted as `+N`.

Если поиск по именам уже успели написать, агент заменит его.

- `case.yaml` (optional): schema_version: "1.1", name, tags, runs, execution: {prompt, model, max_turns, ...}, context: {scaffold_script, history_file, add_dirs}, graders: [{name, type, ...}] (for llm put the rubric in `criteria`). prompt.md frontmatter overrides it; graders/*.md are added after.
- `graders/<name>.md`: frontmatter `type`, `weight` (default 1), `arm` (with-only | both), plus the options below. Types:
  - regex: pattern (JS regex), flags (e.g. i), match (contains | not_contains | "count:N"), target.
  - tool_used: tool, input_match (regex over the JSON input), min (default 1), max; never called = min 0 and max 0. A `Skill` check: tool: Skill, input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?<skill-name>"'.
  - tool_order: before, after (tool name or {tool, input_match}).
  - file_exists: path (glob of files Claude created), exists (default true).
  - llm: criteria (the file body), focus; concrete PASS/FAIL conditions, short outputs only.
  - baseline: baseline_file (.jsonl in the case dir), criteria.
- target (regex) and focus (llm): last_message (default) | trace | files (created paths) | { source: file, path: <file in workspace after the run> } | mock_calls.
- MCP mocks: `evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md` (or the case's own `mocks/`): body = tool result, with {{input.<field>}}; frontmatter type (fixed | agent), expect, error. A tool without a mock is unavailable.
- Prefer one grader on the result and one on the steps (tool_used/tool_order); use regex over llm whenever possible.

# Reporting
After each phase or task tell the user briefly: what changed (files), how it was verified (eval result or check), what is left or uncertain, and the proposed next step. If something failed or was skipped, say so plainly.

input.message:
Finding: no explicit baseline marker exists, in either repo. The app infers baselines from run data. App source is on disk at /Users/KillBill/Documents/projects/plugin-master (apps/server, apps/web, libs/protocol).

How the UI recognises a baseline (apps/server/src/evals/suites.ts):
- :127 `const isMain = (rs) => mainPlugin !== undefined && rs[0]?.plugin === mainPlugin;`
- :131-132 `kindOf = isMain(rs) ? 'main' : rs.some(r => r.cases.some(c => mainNames.has(c.name))) ? 'baseline' : 'other'`
- Meaning: a suite whose plugin name differs from the main plugin, but which shares case names with a main suite, is a "baseline" suite.
- The main plugin name comes from `pluginName(root)` (results.ts:185).
- Each run's plugin is read from `aggregate-result.json` at `suite.plugins[0].name` (results.ts:163). The version comes from `suite.plugins[0].version` (results.ts:78).
- Suites are keyed by plugin name + the common parent dir of the case dirs (suites.ts:56-60).
- Baseline runs are collected per case name (suites.ts:134-148) and need `c.score !== undefined`.
- Auto-pick is `pickBaseline` (suites.ts:66-72): the latest baseline run of the same case and the same `model` that started at or before the main run, otherwise the nearest later one. It matches on `run.model`, which is `suite.modelOverride` (groups.ts:12).
- Other ways a baseline shows up:
  - For a main run whose case has `c.without.score` (ablation arm), that arm is the baseline (suites.ts:158-161).
  - The Baseline column is `c.latest.baselineScore` (apps/web/src/features/evals/columns.tsx:175).
  - Kind enum: libs/protocol/src/lib/evals.ts:235 `kind: z.enum(['main','baseline','other'])`.

Shape of a marked entry: there is none. There is no per-run flag, no "baselineId" and no "isBaseline" (grepped apps, libs, docs).
- A run counts as a baseline only through its own `aggregate-result.json` fields: `suite.plugins[0].name` differing from the main plugin, matching `cases[].name` values, `cases[].score`, and `suite.modelOverride`.
- `docs/tuning-research.md:166` says "baseline is 'latest result of same cases', not a pinned commit". A pinned baseline is a planned idea, not implemented.

In ambicode:
- `.plugin-master/config.json` has only masterContext, activePlan, evalTrusted and features. No baseline field.
- `evals/history.jsonl` and `evals/cases/results/plugin.json` have 0 matches for "baseline".
- `aggregate-result.json` for 2026-10-20T21-55-10-444Z has `suite.plugins[0]` = {name: "ambicode", version: "0.6.2"}, `suite.modelOverride` "claude-sonnet-5-5", `suite.ablation` "none". No marker.
- evals/scripts/*.mjs only mention baseline in comments (run.mjs:99, init-cases.mjs:97,152,289). evals/README.md:4 says the bare arm (no plugin) "is the baseline". The case-level grader `type: baseline` with `baseline_file` (.jsonl) is a different thing (.plugin-master/MASTER.md:62).
- The only "baseline" marking is prose. The sonnet v2 stamps 2026-10-20T21-55-10..22-01-24 are declared the init/scout baseline in `.plugin-master/STATE.md:161` and `.plugin-master/plans/d4083a5a.json:88`. The app does not read either.

Practical consequence: marking a run in JSON would need a new app field. Without app changes, the closest existing mechanism is the bare/ablation arm (`cases[].without`) or a run under a different plugin name with the same case names.

I did not look at apps/web hooks or docs/eval-plan.md for any UI override beyond `compareWith` / `initialBaseline` in EvalRunView.tsx:55,257 and EvalCompare. That is a UI-only selection of a run id, not persisted in JSON that I saw.
